# SUMMARY OF THE INDIVIDUAL BOOKS
->*of this Treatise.*<-

BOOK 1. Concerning the Egyptian Hieroglyphic Gods: Osiris, Isis, Mercury, Vulcan, Typhon, etc.; and concerning the wondrous works of the Kings, the characteristics of individual living creatures, and other monuments pertaining to this subject. <note>The author views Egyptian mythology as a coded language for natural philosophy.</note>

BOOK 2. Concerning the allegories of the Greeks, especially the "golden" ones—such as the Golden Fleece of Jason, the Golden Apples of the Hesperides, etc.—denoting nothing other than the "golden medicine." <note>The "golden medicine" refers to the Philosopher's Stone or the Universal Panacea.</note>

BOOK 3. Concerning the fictitious genealogy of the gods and goddesses, which is Philosophical or Chemico-Medical in nature. <term>Philosophical: in this context, referring to Alchemy, often called the "Hermetic Philosophy."</term>

BOOK 4. Concerning the festivals and sacred rites, as well as the contests and games, established for the sake of this science.

BOOK 5. Concerning the Labors of Hercules, signifying the very same craftsmanship <note>original: "artificium"</note> of the Great Work.

BOOK 6. Concerning the Trojan expedition and the requirements without which Troy could not be captured, and the wanderings of Ulysses, pertaining to the same matter.

# FRONTISPIECE

->[An elaborate copperplate engraving featuring an architectural frame.]<-

<image-desc>
Two fluted **columns** <note>In alchemical symbolism, columns often represent the "pillars of the art," signifying stability, strength, and the dual principles (such as Sol and Luna) that support the work.</note> stand firmly upon a stepped pedestal base. Each column is topped with a large, smooth **sphere**, likely representing the macrocosm (the universe) and the microcosm (man). 

At the summit of the composition, a male figure—**Mercury** <note>Original: *Mercurius*. The Roman messenger god, known to the Greeks as Hermes. In this context, he is the patron of the "Hermetic Art" (alchemy) and represents the elusive element mercury, or "quicksilver."</note>—sits atop a jagged mountain range. He wears a flowing cloak and holds the **caduceus** aloft in his right hand. 

<term>Caduceus: a herald's staff entwined by two serpents, symbolizing the union of opposing forces (like sulfur and mercury) and the resolution of conflict into harmony.</term>

Billowing clouds fill the sky behind the mountains, suggesting a divine or ethereal realm. The central space between the columns and the mountain range remains blank, though faint markings from the text on the reverse side are visible through the paper.
</image-desc>

<note>The mountain depicted here is often interpreted in alchemical texts as the "Philosophical Mountain," a place of difficult ascent where the primary materials for the Philosopher's Stone are discovered.</note>

## The Author’s Six-Line Verse to the Kind Reader
-> Distinguishing between the Fault-finder and the Buffoon. <-

> The Daughter of **SATURN** <note>Original: *Saturni Filia*. In classical tradition, Truth (*Veritas*) was said to be the daughter of Saturn (Time). In the alchemical context, this suggests that "Truth" is being extracted from the "darkness" of Saturn, which represents lead or the raw, unrefined state of matter.</note> is rescued from the shadows by our effort,
> And, brought forth anew through labor, she is given to the light;
> Behold, O kind reader, she is carried into your arms,
> If you will not be an unjust judge in your assessment.
> **NOTHING IS EASIER** than for critics <note>Original: *Momis*. Referring to Momus, the Greek god of mockery and blame, who famously found fault with everything, even the works of the gods.</note> to despise even the best of things;
> **NOTHING IS HARDER** than to produce works that might please the entertainers. <note>Original: *Mimis*. Referring to "mimes" or jesters; here, the author refers to those who look for superficial or trivial amusement rather than the "heavy" work of true philosophy.</note>

<term>Hexastichon: A poem or stanza consisting of exactly six lines.</term>

<summary>In this introductory poem, the author presents his work as the "Daughter of Saturn" (Truth) rescued from darkness, asking the reader for a fair judgment. He contrasts the "kind reader" with the cynical critic (Momus) and the trivial entertainer (Mimus), noting that destruction is easy while creation is difficult.</summary>

# MICHAEL MA-
## IER, COUNT PALATINE OF THE IMPERIAL COURT <note>Original: *Comitis Pal. Cæs.* Michael Maier (1568–1622) was a physician and counselor to Holy Roman Emperor Rudolf II, who granted him this noble title.</note>
### PREFACE TO THE READERS.

<image-desc>A large historiated woodcut initial 'S' within a square frame, decorated with intricate vine and foliage motifs.</image-desc>

*If you wonder, kind readers, what cause arose for me, why I published this treatise distinguished by the name of <term>MOST SECRET THINGS</term> <note>Original: *Arcanissimorum*. This refers to the "Arcana," or deep secrets of nature and alchemy that are hidden from the uninitiated.</note> after so many and such great authors on hieroglyphics, allegories, fables, theological, philosophical, poetic, alchemical, and medical matters have been made common, and have now at last scattered it into the public light of the world, and dedicated it especially to you for judgment out of so many preconceived notions—once you have looked at the matter itself, my studies and my mind, and your own openness of spirit together, you will without doubt cease to wonder. Among Christians, I believe, there is no one so unskilled in all things—if only they possess common sense and hold the first rudiments of letters—who has not at some time read the books of the Pagans <note>Original: *Ethnicorum*. Maier uses this term to refer to the pre-Christian Greeks and Romans.</note> (of which a huge number has reached our age) and has not observed these two things in them: First, the names of gods, goddesses, and heroes, such as Jupiter, Mars, Mercury, Apollo, Juno, Venus, Pallas, Hercules, Jason, and the rest; Second, the monstrous, horrific, and incredible deeds of the individual gods and heroes. For with these two things all the books of the Pagans are so filled that on almost every page, by insisting on them, they contain hardly anything else worthy of memory. For example, if someone were to take away the gods and the deeds of the gods and the heroes born from gods from Homer and Herodotus among the Greeks, or from Livy and Virgil among the Romans, the largest part of their works would be marked with a critical dagger <note>Original: *obelisco*. In ancient scholarship, an "obelisk" or dagger symbol was used in the margins of manuscripts to mark passages that were considered fake, doubtful, or superfluous.</note>: For the deeds are so tied to the persons, and the persons to the deeds, that if one is removed, the other cannot stand,*

<sig>A</sig>

<summary>Michael Maier introduces his preface by addressing why he is publishing another work on ancient myths, arguing that the core of classical Greek and Roman literature is inextricably bound to the "monstrous" and "incredible" stories of gods and heroes.</summary>
<keywords>Michael Maier, Preface, Alchemy, Greek Mythology, Roman Mythology, Hieroglyphics, Homer, Virgil, Arcanissima</keywords>

# PREFACE
<meta>catchword: non</meta>

*...if one thing is granted, let the other also be granted: the same judgment applies to other <term>Pagan</term> <note>Original: *Ethnicis*. In this context, Maier refers to the pre-Christian Greeks and Romans.</note> authors and their writings. But we Christians have long since cast away, mocked, and ridiculed that multitude of gods, being instructed by the truth of the Word of God <note>Original: *Verbi Dei*.</note>: What then shall we say of so many deeds of gods and heroes? Are these things possible and true, when their authors were not gods and were false? Or shall we indeed refute and reject the gods, yet nonetheless admit and receive their deeds and progeny? Or shall we pronounce these things false along with the gods, and claim there is no truth in either among any of the authors? It is strange that no one among so many myriads of writing Christians has been concerned about this, even though the explanation of these difficulties is so necessary that hardly any writing, whether political or <term>Theosophical</term> <note>Original: *Theosophicum*. In the 17th century, this referred to a philosophical system that sought direct knowledge of God and the secrets of nature.</note>, after the Holy Scriptures, could be offered to the world more usefully. But the reason is that those things seem not only most ancient and placed beyond all memory of writers, but also most secret, in that they have always been held regarding their true origin and known to very few: For those things ought by right to be judged the most ancient and at the same time the* **MOST SECRET** <note>Original: *ARCANISSIMA*. This is the central theme of Maier's book—the "secrets of secrets."</note> *which through so many ages of the world—more than three thousand years—from the first authors up to our own times, have been covered and hidden like a treasure most secretly shut in a chest. Concerning these, although the Pagan writers have unfolded some things, albeit fabulous in a fabulous manner—that is, according to their own capacity—they called them mysteries, as is clear from the titles of the books of Eumolpus, Menander, Melanthius, Iamblichus, Evanthis, and others <note>Maier lists several classical and Neoplatonist authors who wrote on religious mysteries and myths.</note> containing nothing besides poetic fables, and not truly explaining even a tiny bit of them; for the reason that they understood that great and mystical things lie hidden under these fictions, containing in truth more in their depths than they promise at first glance. For the ancient Egyptians, most wise men (from whom, if we trace back the first origin, we will notice all these things have been spread), when they had attained most precious things by the gift of GOD and their own labor, which they did not want to be entirely unknown to posterity, nor yet equally known to everyone, found a way of obscuring them, and as if wrapping them in certain darkness, so that...*

<summary>Maier argues that while Christians rightly reject pagan gods, the ancient myths contain hidden, "most secret" physical and philosophical truths. He traces these secrets back to the ancient Egyptians, who intentionally obscured their discoveries to protect them from the uninitiated.</summary>

<keywords>Egyptian wisdom, Pagan mythology, Christian interpretation, Arcanissima, mysteries, hermeticism, Michael Maier, secret knowledge</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the preface where Michael Maier argues that ancient myths were intentionally designed as "prisons" for secret knowledge to prevent the uninitiated from understanding them too easily. He is transitioning from the general concept of secrecy to the historical consequences of misinterpreting these "secrets."</meta>

### To the Readers.

...only those endowed with the sharpest light of the mind might suspect anything of their true nature. Thus, they devised <term>hieroglyphic characters</term> <note>Original: *Hieroglypha grammata*. In the 17th century, hieroglyphs were viewed not just as writing, but as mystical symbols that encoded deep philosophical or chemical truths.</note>, allegories, and fables. These served as enclosures or prisons to confine and hide matters that were not to be made public for as long as they wished, so that those seeing or hearing them would not understand immediately, but would at least have reason to investigate the causes. 

But it can hardly be said or believed how much evil has sprung from this. We read that in Babylon, in the temple of Apollo, a golden chest of wondrous antiquity was once found. When it was forced open, a force of pestilential and most ruinous air poured out. This blast did not only strike down those present, infecting them with a poisonous and lethal rot, but it spread with such incredible, plague-like power that it afflicted the <term>Parthians</term> <note>An ancient Iranian empire; the term here refers generally to the peoples of the Near East.</note> far and wide. 

Or as occurred during the reigns of Marcus Antonius and Verus at Seleucia: after the temple of Apollo was plundered and his statue moved to Rome, some soldiers opened a narrow hole that the <term>Chaldean</term> <note>Priest-interpreters of Mesopotamia, often associated with astrology and hidden wisdom.</note> priests had previously sealed. A fatal and most foul vapor emerged, raging furiously from the borders of Persia through Syria, all of Greece, and its neighboring regions as far as Gaul (as Ammianus Marcellinus and, following him, <term>Caelius Rhodiginus</term> <note>Ludovicus Ricchierius, a Renaissance scholar known for his encyclopedic "Ancient Lessons" (*Lectiones Antiquae*).</note> recount in Book 5, Chapter 12). 

In almost the same way, the treasures of the Egyptians were hidden under their secret coverings. When they were opened in an improper manner, they filled all of Greece—and later the whole world—with superstitions, a multitude of the vainest gods, and astounding tales. This evil persisted throughout the entire era of <term>Paganism</term>, until the true Physician of the soul, our **SAVIOR**, arrived. He provided for the human race with a remedy far different from that of Hippocrates (who saved the Athenians from a plague by burning forests). Our Savior utterly ruined and destroyed those idols of the nations by the most secret, saving **WORD** brought forth from the heart of the **ETERNAL FATHER**. 

Since then, the gods of the nations have long been seen as worthless in the Church and the Christian world—rejected as fictitious and vain. Yet, because so many monuments and books of the <term>Pagans</term> <note>Original: *Ethnicorum*.</note> are nonetheless published every day...

<meta>catchword: in</meta>

<summary>Maier compares the "opening" of Egyptian secrets by the Greeks to a plague released from a cursed chest, arguing that improper interpretation led to the spread of pagan superstition until the arrival of Christ. He suggests that while the gods themselves are false, the "secret coverings" of their stories still merit investigation.</summary>

# Preface
A

...they circulate in the hands of the learned, in almost every paragraph of which mention is made of the pagan gods and heroes. This has given scholars a reason to diligently investigate what exactly was understood by those gods and heroes. Therefore, some have been found who reduced them partly to **history**, as if those gods and heroes were kings and men in ancient times <note>This approach is known as **Euhemerism**, the theory that the gods were originally historical human beings who were later deified due to their great deeds.</note> and performed such great things as are written about them. Others have applied these stories to the shaping of **morals** or to the **natural order** of this world. 

But since these interpreters have frequently brought forth the most absurd ideas—neither worthy of those first very wise men to wrap up in mystery, nor worthy of the interpreters themselves to unwrap—and have corrupted the greater part of these stories with their own fictions produced without any agreement of the facts, they have left more doubt than certainty in the minds of readers. 

Consequently, many have wished that what truly lay beneath those gods and heroes of the nations were thoroughly expressed. For it is surely credible that something did not originate as a trivial matter—arising merely from history or to be stretched toward moral lessons—which has involved almost the whole world and so many wise men within it, not just for a hundred years (which would be too much), but for thirty times a hundred or more, that is, **three thousand years**. It has held them involved and blinded them. 

Meanwhile, among those who treat <term>chemical</term> <note>Original: *chymica*. At this time, "chemistry" and "alchemy" were often used interchangeably, though Maier will soon make a sharp distinction between the two.</note> matters, some have come forward who affirm that the pagan gods and goddesses took their first origin from chemical works. Among these were <term>Braceschus</term> <note>Giovanni Battista Bracesco, a 16th-century Italian author who wrote dialogues claiming that ancient myths hidden in the works of Geber and Lully were actually chemical instructions.</note>, <term>Rob. Vallensis</term> <note>Robertus Vallensis (Robert Duval), an early historian of alchemy who sought to prove the antiquity of the art by linking it to ancient Greek and Roman poetry.</note>, and several others. 

But since these authors partly accommodated everything to their own private concerns, and did not sufficiently provide the underlying reason and harmony of all things in a suitable method—and because <term>chemistry</term> itself is held by many to be vain, futile, and useless—nothing certain could be determined by the learned regarding these matters. 

For this reason, I have finally taken this work upon myself, led by various causes: namely, to declare and place before the eyes of readers in a single treatise what things were originally understood by the gods, goddesses, and heroes of the nations, and by what means those fables have been propagated through the ages of the world until now. I do this both so that the truth of **Christian doctrine**, which shines brightly enough on its own, may be further illustrated once these shadows are removed, and so that **Chemistry**—not **Alchemy** <note>Original: *Alcumia*. Maier uses this term pejoratively to describe the "puffers" or fraudulent alchemists who sought only to make common gold through deception.</note> (that nurse of so many scoundrels and mother of deceptions, which adulterates metals and does not truly transmute them), but that which serves the production of the <term>Golden Medicine</term> <note>Original: *Medicina Aurea*. This refers to the universal panacea or the Philosopher's Stone, intended for healing the body as well as perfecting metals.</note>—may be demonstrated to be most ancient and most true...
<column-break/>

# To the Readers.
### A 3

...be demonstrated, and **SO GREAT A GIFT OF GOD** may be vindicated from the blasphemies of detractors. No one, I believe, will judge gold—that most excellent metal, which for its value has been accepted in the world as long as the world has existed and will exist, and which is often used to cure many human diseases—as useless, most harmful, and detestable, or proscribe and accuse it, simply because he does not possess as great a supply of it as he would wish. Nor will he reject it because it does not remove all the passions, diseases, and desires of men, or because it is the enticing cause of the perpetration of many evils—theft, robbery, homicide, adultery, and almost all vices—unless he wishes to live entirely outside the world and appear as a **Cynic** <note>The Cynics were ancient Greek philosophers who famously rejected wealth and social conventions in favor of a simple, often harsh, life.</note>. 

Let the same judgment apply to Medicine: if, therefore, a medicine comes from gold, or from this essence of gold, who but the most insane person would detest that medicine? He is a child in the world who thinks everything is the same everywhere as it is in his own house, city, or region where he was raised. He is twice a child who, though of mature age, thinks there have never been nor are any who have seen, known, and understood more in things than he himself can grasp. Therefore, no one of sound judgment will deny the truth of **Chymistry** <note>original: "Chymiae". In the 17th century, the term "Chymistry" encompassed both what we now distinguish as chemistry and alchemy.</note> simply because he does not see, know, or understand it. For this would be a mark of a most shameless mind: to wish to accept only those entities known to oneself and to banish the unknown from the universe. This, I say, would be an envious and dog-like <note>The Latin *canini* suggests a "cynical" or snarling attitude, like a dog that prevents others from enjoying what it cannot use itself.</note> habit, not a human one—to take away from the world that which he himself cannot use. 

But lest anyone should think that I, in putting forth such a writing, profess to have a complete knowledge of this same subject, let him understand the reasoning of my studies. Having practiced **Galenic medicine** <note>The traditional medical system based on the teachings of the 2nd-century physician Galen, focusing on the balance of the four bodily "humors."</note> until now, I have not ceased to investigate other matters—if there be any—that are most secret within the field of Chymistry. For I have judged this to be characteristic of a liberally educated man, since just as birds seem born to fly, so he seems born to reason. We see that the entire sky, not just one part of the air, is open to birds; why should it not be so for men regarding their reasoning? Therefore, let no one be angry with me if, beyond common knowledge, I desire to know even the secret and rare things that have their foundation in the nature of things, proven by reason and experience, and most true. For **Aristotle** demonstrates in his **Metaphysics** <note>Aristotle’s *Metaphysics* famously begins with the statement: "All men by nature desire to know."</note> that this is characteristic of an intelligent soul. Indeed, spurred on by this passion, I have also visited foreign places, and thus [I arrived] also in this most celebrated kingdom...

<meta>catchword: I arrived,</meta>

<summary>Maier defends alchemy (Chymistry) and the pursuit of hidden natural secrets, arguing that ignorance is no reason to deny their truth. He positions his own research as a natural extension of his Galenic medical training and his travels to "celebrated" foreign lands.</summary>
<keywords>Alchemy, Galenic Medicine, Aristotle, Metaphysics, Chymistry, Gold, Scientific inquiry, Cynicism</keywords>

# Preface

I reached a point where, while I was intensely focused on advancing my studies, behold: this "offspring" was born to me. Conceived by the pen, it is not a mere servant, but a precursor to that Medicine I have been investigating until now. Yet it is not so premature as one might imagine, as if it could not survive; indeed, I have nurtured it within myself longer than elephants are said to carry their young in the womb. I confess I have now sent it forth into the light by a "bear-birth" <note>original: *ursino partu*. An ancient belief that bear cubs were born as shapeless lumps and licked into form by their mothers; used here to describe a work that still needs polishing.</note> and with unrefined wisdom <note>original: *rudi Minerva*. A Latin idiom meaning a work produced with simple wit or without great artistic polish.</note>. For this work is not so concerned with mere words as with the reality of things, nor with seeking a bit of glory for myself, but rather with providing benefit to others.

Therefore, kind readers, accept this work of mine, such as it is—a new labor in this field. Just as true Theology cannot be seen as unnecessary, so too will this work be extremely useful to the entire <term>Encyclopedia</term> <note>From the Greek *enkyklios paideia*, meaning the "circle of learning" or the complete system of knowledge, rather than a modern reference book.</note> of knowledge, including Politics and civil life (the domain of Law), Medicine, Chymistry, Poetry, History, Astronomy, Physics, and all other sciences and arts. And although it may seem to contain paradoxes because it challenges ideas accepted for so many centuries, I believe that what aligns with truth in all matters—even if it differs from the opinions of the majority—is more worthy of being embraced than anything that merely conforms to the prejudices of the masses. 

Since we follow this principle in divine matters, why should we not also do so in those human affairs that are considered to come closest to them (as these do)? If anyone prefers to approve of Paganism and the multitude of gods, failing to recognize the true Chymistry <note>original: *Chymiam*. Here referring to the alchemical and natural secrets the author believes are hidden within ancient myths.</note> within these myths—even if it remains unknown to him—and pleases himself with a certain sharp-tongued criticism, let him do as he likes. In the meantime, he will never make the falsehood of the pagans seem likely, nor the truth of this art seem empty to those who truly understand. 

You, who carry a spark of Promethean light in your breast and the wisdom of Pallas Athena in your soul—even if you do not share a common altar with those who worship Vulcan <note>The Roman god of fire and metalworking, associated here with the literal fire of the alchemical furnace.</note> or Vesta <note>The goddess of the hearth and domestic fire.</note>—I ask you, in your integrity, to defend this study of ours from the insults of the envious and the "scourgers" <note>original: *mastygum*. From the Greek *mastix*, meaning a whip; refers here to harsh, lashing critics.</note>. Take care to do your utmost to dig out and extract Truth from that deep well or cave in which she is buried—a depth to which Democritus <note>The "Laughing Philosopher," who famously claimed that truth lies at the bottom of a well.</note> testified with laughter and Heracletus <note>The "Weeping Philosopher."</note> with tears. ### Book 1 of the Hieroglyphics

...useful for life, as the foreign writers call them.

<margin>Book 1, chapter 2. The First Gods.</margin>
The same author narrates, shortly in the following chapter, that the Sun and Moon were worshipped by the first men as eternal Gods, and that for a specific reason of naming, the former was called *Osiris* and the latter *Isis*. However, who the one and true God of Gods is, and when and where the first humans and kings on earth emerged, we have received as indubitable truth from the Holy Bible. Consequently, we recognize the vanity of the *Egyptians* in this matter, as well as in their assertion of the antiquity of their kings and a numerical series continued through more than twenty thousand years. Since they say elsewhere that *Isis* and *Osiris* were born from *Saturn* <note>In alchemy and mythology, Saturn often represents primeval matter or the beginning of a process.</note>, it is a wonder why they consider them the first eternal and unbegotten gods, or celestial lights. We can, however, excuse the Pagan writers if they handed down matters differently than they truly are, both because their true nature could not be known due to their antiquity—the sacred history of *Moses* being unknown to them—and because they were not permitted to think otherwise due to the accepted religion of the Gods at that time. 

<margin>The proposition and summary of the entire treatise.</margin>
As we establish the foundation of *Egyptian* doctrine, we have determined through innumerable signs that throughout all of *Egypt*, a certain science teaching the most secret works of nature—namely, the **GOLDEN MEDICINE** <term>Medicina Aurea: A central concept in alchemy referring to the "Universal Medicine" or the Philosopher's Stone, which was believed to cure all diseases and transmute base metals into gold.</term>, not made of gold, but a thousand times more precious than gold—was in use, especially among the most ancient Philosophers, Priests, and Kings. So that this science might be passed down to the wiser posterity while remaining unknown to the common people, they employed hidden signs taken from animals for their writing, later called *Hieroglyphics* by the Greeks. For the explanation of things, they everywhere utilized Allegories transferred from fictional persons and their deeds. Hence, in succeeding times, as the minds of ignorant men were preoccupied by superstition, those persons were regarded as Gods or kings, and animals were worshipped as sacred and inviolable.

### Book I of Hieroglyphics

...were mortals, but indeed attained immortality through their wisdom and the benefits they provided to the human race. Some of these reigned in *Egypt*, and were called partly by the names of the celestial Gods and partly by their own: the *Sun, Saturn, Rhea, Jupiter* (also called *Ammon* by some), *Juno, Vulcan, Vesta*, and finally *Mercury*. Indeed, the first king among the *Egyptians* was the *Sun*, sharing the same name as the celestial star.

<margin>The inventions of Vulcan.</margin>
Certain priests affirm that *Vulcan* <note>The Roman name for the Greek Hephaestus, the god of fire and smithing</note> reigned first, as he was the inventor of fire; because of this benefit, he was appointed leader by the *Egyptians*. And a little later: They say that next came *Saturn*, who took his sister *Rhea* as his wife, and according to some, they fathered *Osiris* and *Isis*; however, many report that they fathered *Jupiter* and *Juno*, who ruled over the entire world because of their virtue. These five gods were born on the days the *Egyptians* call intercalary <note>original: *intercalares*; the five extra days added to the Egyptian calendar to complete the solar year</note>: *Osiris, Isis, Typhon, Apollo,* and *Venus*. Furthermore, *Osiris* is interpreted as *Dionysus*, and *Isis* as *Ceres*. Once *Osiris* took her as his wife and assumed the kingdom, he contributed many things to the use of common life.

<margin>The inventions of Isis.</margin>
The author <note>Referring to the Greek historian Diodorus Siculus, whom Maier is paraphrasing</note> then relates that *Isis* discovered wheat and barley and taught men how to sow them. She also gave laws and erected a temple to her parents, *Jupiter* and *Juno*, which was notable for both its size and its adornment. Furthermore, she established two golden Temples: one larger for *Celestial Jupiter*, and the other smaller for *King Jupiter* their father, whom some call *Ammon*. In the same passage, *Diodorus* says she also built golden temples for others whom we have mentioned, with honors and priests established for each. The discoverers of arts or things pertaining to the utility of life were also held in honor by *Osiris* and *Isis*. Moreover, smiths of copper and gold were discovered in the *Thebaid* <note>The region surrounding the ancient city of Thebes in Upper Egypt</note>, and weapons were made with which they could both kill wild beasts and cultivate the land. Additionally, statues and golden temples of the Gods were manufactured by them with every refinement.

# Book I: Of Egyptians and Greeks

...[to letters and] they say he gave names to things; they also say he was the inventor of letters and established with what honor and by what sacred rites the gods should be worshipped. He was especially an observer of the courses of the stars and discovered the harmonies of voices. They report him as the discoverer of wrestling, of numbers, and of the medical art for curing bodies; furthermore, he was the inventor of the lyre made of three strings, representing the three seasons of the year. ### Book I of Hieroglyphics

Egyptian letters were introduced: He <note>Referring to Hermes/Mercury</note> taught rhetoric, astronomy, geometry, arithmetic, and music. For nothing is done in art, just as in nature, without **number, weight, and measure** <note>original: "numero, pondere & mensura"; a reference to the biblical Book of Wisdom 11:20, frequently cited by alchemists to justify the mathematical precision of their work</note>. Thus says **Ramon Llull** <note>A 13th-century Majorcan philosopher and polymath whose works became central to later alchemical tradition</note> in the *Theory of the Testament*, Chapter 50: "Nature," he says, "contains within itself the philosophy and science of the **seven liberal arts** <note>The traditional curriculum of medieval education: grammar, logic, rhetoric, arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy</note>, by which it operates. For nature herself carries every geometric form and defines every thing by the power of her arithmetic through the equality of a certain number; and through rhetorical knowledge, she leads your intellect from potentiality into action." So says he. 

**Mercury** himself is the interpreter of all things, called **Hermes** by the Greeks, whose counsel **Osiris** uses most extensively; because without Mercury, nothing is done. To him belongs the sacred olive, as it is the most excellent of all oils, which is able to harden things that are too soft and soften those that are hard, by one and the same fire. Other matters regarding **Mercury** and **Vulcan** will be explained in the following pages. 

But why did **Isis** establish everything from gold—even entire temples—for her parent and the other gods? Especially since in any other age it is unheard of for even a single temple to be built entirely of gold, particularly in these more recent times, where the abundance of gold dug from mines and rivers is a thousand times greater than in ancient times, when gold is said to have first been found. Or why did Isis hold the smiths of bronze and gold in such high honor? 

The cause is ready at hand: she is surely the **Golden Goddess**. She is also said to be the sister and wife of **Osiris**, just as **Juno** is to **Jupiter** and **Rhea** to **Saturn**, who are described as their progenitors. This is the single most evident and characteristic sign of <term>Chemistry; Chymia, here referring to the "Great Art" of alchemy</term>; its subject consists of a male "agent" and a female "patient," like a brother and sister, and also like a married couple, as will be demonstrated throughout this work. 

**Osiris**, therefore, and **Isis**, just like **Vulcan** and **Mercury**, are the principal intellectual chemical gods—not celestial, but subterranean, and born from Art. Since **Isis** is **Ceres** <note>The Roman goddess of agriculture</note> and **Osiris** is **Bacchus** or **Dionysus** among the Greeks, we will provide their other qualities and characteristics below. Indeed, as **Diodorus** <note>Diodorus Siculus, a Greek historian</note> relates in the same passage: since **Osiris** was a good man and eager for glory, he gathered a huge army so that he might travel across the world and teach mortals the plan[ting]—

# Book I. Of the Egyptian-Greeks

...to plant vines, as well as harvests of wheat and barley, and the offspring of livestock. He believed that if he could lead men from a wild existence to a more refined and gentle one, he would obtain immortal honors—which indeed he achieved. For not only those men of old, but even later generations, mindful of the benefit of the crops he discovered, held him as one of the greatest gods. 

They report that once the kingdom of Egypt was established, Osiris entrusted the care of all affairs to his wife **Isis**. He assigned **Mercury** to her so that she might use his counsel, as he was seen to excel in wisdom among his companions. As leader of the army and of all things under his dominion, he left **Hercules**, both because he was his closest kinsman and because of his admirable courage and physical strength. 

He divided the governance of the kingdom in this way: he placed **Busiris** over Phoenicia and the coastal regions, and **Antaeus** <note>In Greek mythology, a giant who was invincible as long as he touched the earth; here, he is presented as a historical governor under Osiris</note> over the lands neighboring Ethiopia and Libya. He himself set out from Egypt on an expedition with all his forces, taking with him his brother, whom the Greeks call **Apollo**, the discoverer of the laurel tree. Two sons, unequal in character, *Anubis* and *Macedon*, followed Osiris; each used notable heraldry featuring an animal not unlike their own nature. For *Anubis* bore a dog and *Macedon* a wolf as their military standards. For this reason, the Egyptians hold these animals in the highest honor, and they are worshipped among them in the forms of these creatures. 

He also brought with him **Pan**, for whom the Egyptians built a city in the Thebaid bearing his name, called **Chemmis**, which is to say, the City of **Pan**. Those skilled in agriculture also followed him: **Maron**, who knew how to plant vineyards, and **Triptolemus**, who knew how to sow wheat. Once everything was settled and prayers were offered to the gods, they say that **Osiris** let his hair grow until such time as he should return to Egypt, and then set out toward Ethiopia. 

While in Ethiopia, it is said that **Satyrs** <note>original: "Satyros"; mythical creatures usually depicted as half-man and half-goat, often representing the wild forces of nature</note> were presented to him, having hair that reached down to their navels. Osiris is said to have been quite fond of laughter and was accustomed to taking delight in music and dance. For this reason, a great company of musicians followed him. Among them were nine young maidens, skilled both in song and other branches of learning, whom the Greeks thereafter called

# Book I of Hieroglyphics

...the Muses: They say that *Apollo* taught them, which is why he was named the Musician <note>original: "Musicus"</note>. At this time, they say that around the rising of the Dog Star, *Sirius* (for that is when it is most accustomed to grow), the *Nile* flooded the greater part of *Egypt*, especially that part over which *Prometheus* ruled. With almost all the inhabitants of that region destroyed, they say *Prometheus* was moved by such grief that he wished to kill himself. Because of the swiftness of its current and the depth of its waters, the river was then called the *Eagle* <note>original: "Aquilam"; this explains the myth of the eagle "devouring" Prometheus as an allegory for a flood destroying his land</note>. *Hercules*, however, through his great wisdom and courage, is said to have immediately checked the rush of the waters and turned them back to their former course. 

But *Osiris*, while he was in the mountains of *Ethiopia*, lined both banks of the *Nile* with dikes so that the flood would not exceed its bounds, but rather, by passing through certain gates, it would be gentle and beneficial to the fields. Then, making his way through *Arabia* along the Red Sea, he reached the furthest *Indians*, where he founded many cities; one of these he named *Nysa*, in memory of the place where he had been raised <note>In myth, Nysa is the legendary mountain where Dionysus/Osiris was nursed by nymphs</note>. There he planted ivy, which is the only place in that region where it grows, as well as in the *Nysa* of *Egypt*. He also left many other monuments of his presence among the *Indians*, even setting up columns in many places as witnesses to his expedition. 

He then traversed the other nations of *Asia*; crossing into *Europe* via the *Hellespont*, he slew *Lycurgus*, the king of the Thracian barbarians, who opposed him. Over that province he placed the elderly *Maro* in charge; he appointed his son *Macedon* as king of *Macedonia*, and he placed *Triptolemus* in charge of cultivating the fields of Attica. Finally, when he had traveled almost the entire world, he returned to *Egypt*, bringing with him gifts given by various nations. Then, when he was translated from the rank of men to the Gods, honors and sacred rites were established for him as the greatest of the Gods by *Isis* and *Mercury* <note>Hermes</note>.

<margin>Mystical matters.</margin>
Many things were added to his worship with mystical power, by which they might make the power of that God more magnificent. Let it suffice to have briefly cited these things from *Diodorus* <note>Diodorus Siculus, a 1st-century BCE Greek historian</note> regarding the expedition of *Osiris* into *India*. All these narratives are "Hieroglyphic" or allegorical, and if they are understood in any way other than this, they are entirely contrary to the truth—as is evident both from individual details that are literally absurd and false, and from the stories of the planting of wine, the sowing of wheat and barley, and the breeding of livestock...

Moreover, to make the Priests more ready to perform these things through a greater benefit, she granted them a third part of the lands for the cult of the Gods and for sacred rites. The Priests, both mindful of the merits of **Osiris** and attracted by the benefit granted by **Isis**, carried out her commands; because of this, even now every priest testifies that **Osiris** is buried with him.

...many other indications should be brought forward here, which we now pass over in silence. We shall therefore look to explaining the Allegories and Hieroglyphics, at least very briefly.

<margin>What Osiris is</margin>
**Osiris**, as has been said, is held without any ambiguity to be the "matter of the art" from which the **Golden Medicine** <note>A term for the Philosopher’s Stone or the universal elixir</note> is composed. This matter, placed in its tomb—that is, the chemical vessel—is torn into many pieces by his brother **Typhon** <note>Set; in alchemy, this represents the process of dissolution or "corruption" of the base matter</note>. These pieces **Isis** collects and unites after the completion of the work, once the combustible sulfur has been separated out.

<margin>What Isis is</margin>
And thus the collection of the parts of **Osiris** performed by **Isis** is the repetition of the same work <note>reiteration of the distillation or sublimation processes</note>, which continues until the power of **Typhon** is extinguished. In its place, the burning Soul of **Osiris** succeeds to such a degree that it very easily draws to itself its mother **Isis**—be she wife or most loving sister—which is the ultimate perfection.

<margin>What Typhon is</margin>
We have already stated what **Typhon** is: namely, a fiery and furious spirit <note>representing corrosive acids or volatile reagents</note> which soon penetrates our **Osiris** and seizes him into its own color, like a poison. This should not happen in the first, but in the final "cooking" <note>the *coctio*, or heat-treatment phase</note>. For the fire lit in the vessel must not be too sharply intensified by **Vulcan** <note>the god of fire, here meaning the external heat of the furnace</note> at the beginning; otherwise, like the fires of Hell, it will burn the entire body of **Osiris**, so that he can never be restored to life by his mother.

<margin>Note.</margin>
Here it must be noted that **Isis** and **Osiris** are one and the same subject, in which there is the male **Osiris** and the female **Isis**; as well as **Osiris** the son and **Isis** the mother; or **Osiris** the brother and **Isis** the sister. Thus, the substance behaves like a **Hermaphrodite** or **Androgyne** <note>In alchemy, the "Rebis" or "Double-Thing," a single substance possessing both active/male and passive/female principles</note>, being used and accepted now for **Osiris** and now for **Isis** because it reflects both sexes, according to the different aspects of the relationship: husband and wife, brother and sister, mother and son.

Since this subject is unique in nature and belongs specifically to **Alchemy** <note>original: *Chymiæ*</note>, and is known to practitioners, to those same people **Osiris** and **Isis** will become known, along with their whole family and the series of their deeds. As for the **Egyptian** priests having the image of **Osiris**, knowing the tomb alone, and asserting it to be among them yet revealing it to no one: this shows nothing other than that they confess—through Allegory—that they are skilled in and possessors of the alchemical art, yet they wish to reveal it to no one except the most worthy.

# Book 1. The Egyptian-Greeks.

If he had grown weary, he undoubtedly would have been forced to reveal the entire art to *Alexander the Great*, who held *Egypt* at that time. Thus, beneath the mythical veils <note>original: *fabulosis involucris*</note> of *Osiris* and *Isis*, they hid the art for as long as they desired. For if it had been publicly established that Osiris and Isis were neither gods nor mortals, then it would follow that Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Mercury, Apollo, Diana, Venus, and Vulcan had never lived or reigned either. Nevertheless, so many and such great sacred rites and honors were performed for each of them. This would have provided an opportunity for the more curious to investigate what was finally understood and hidden beneath those veiled names.

To the Egyptian priests, such transparency seemed entirely irrational and fraught with the greatest danger. Therefore, they were compelled to assert that these figures were not mere gods, but rather men who had been elevated to the rank of the gods. In doing so, they gave *Alexander* a justification: if the major gods celebrated throughout the world through divine worship had originally been men and kings, then he too—though bound by a mortal body—might allow himself to be worshiped and proclaimed as a God.

It is well known from history that, besides the cult of *Osiris* and *Isis*, the Egyptians also paid honors to *Hercules* and established the *Eleusinian* <note>the most famous of the secret religious rites of ancient Greece, originally from Egypt</note> or the most secret rites of *Ceres*, as well as rites for other gods—namely *Vulcan, Mercury, Saturn, Jupiter*, and their like. 

<margin>2. Concerning the principal Philosopher-Kings of Egypt.</margin>

But leaving those matters to be explored elsewhere, we shall now turn our attention to the more famous kings of the Egyptians. Just as the Egyptian priests teach that *Mercury* <note>the Greek name for Thoth, the god of wisdom</note> was the inventor of the sciences and arts, they credit their Kings with the invention of things necessary for daily life. 

In ancient times, as *Diodorus* <note>Diodorus Siculus, a Greek historian</note> notes, kingship was not passed down to the offspring of the rulers. Instead, it was given to those who were seen to have contributed the most to human life—either because the people chose their own kings for the common good, or because it was so decreed in the sacred books. Some tell the tale that gods and heroes first reigned in Egypt for just under eighteen thousand years, and that the last of the gods to hold the throne was Horus, the son of Isis. Mortal men, however, reigned for slightly less than fifteen thousand years, up to the 180th Olympiad <note>a four-year period used in Greek dating</note>, which was when Diodorus traveled to Egypt during the reign of Ptolemy, who was the ninth of that name, also called *Dionysus* <note>Ptolemy XII Auletes</note>. However, it is clear from the chronology of the world that the Egyptian priests...

### Book I. Of the Egyptian-Greeks.

<margin>Note.</margin>
There is no doubt that Busiris, the king of Egypt who founded Thebes, was a Philosopher and a priest of *Vulcan* <note>Latin: *Vulcani*; likely referring to the Egyptian creator god Ptah, whom the Greeks and Romans identified with Vulcan</note>, just like the others. It is hardly likely that the king would have inscribed on his monument the total sum of gold and silver received annually from the metal mines, as if this wealth were eternal and his own property, when it could never fail to decrease; for riches obtained from mines are rarely steady or uniform, but usually change suddenly. Furthermore, Simandyas could not claim these works for himself if he were not their author, but merely their distributor, since that glory would belong equally to his predecessors and descendants. It would seem close to folly to ensure that riches dug out of the earth be carved onto one's tomb after death. Moreover, the sum is so great that it becomes incredible if it is said to be received annually from the mines, because <margin>1,320,000,000 Crowns</margin> it far exceeds a thousand million [units] of gold. 

From this, I would say there is something mystical hidden beneath this, or that a finite number has been put for an infinite one. # Book I: Egyptian-Greeks

Some report the cause of this great devotion <note>original: "pensi causam"; referring to the weight or importance given to the ritual</note> is that the soul of the deceased **Osiris** migrated into a bull; from there, it was passed down and infused into his descendants. Others claim that after **Osiris** was killed by **Typhon** <note>the Greek name for the Egyptian god Set, the brother and murderer of Osiris</note>, Apis collected the limbs of Osiris and placed them inside a wooden cow covered with a white bull’s hide, and for this reason, the city was named Busiris <note>original: "Busiridem"; likely derived from the Egyptian *Pr-Wsjr*, meaning "House of Osiris"</note>. Many other fables are told about Apis which would be tedious to recount individually. However, the Egyptians, by discussing such wondrous things about the honor shown to these animals—things almost beyond belief—have caused no small doubt for those seeking the true reasons behind them.

<margin>Secret Teachings.</margin>
The priests possess certain secret writings, as we have already mentioned. Many of the Egyptians provide three reasons for this worship, the first of which is entirely mythological and suited to the simplicity of the ancients:

<margin>The first mythological cause for worshipping animals.</margin>
They say that the early Gods, when they were few in number and no match for the strength of the populace, feared the impiety of men. Thus, they disguised themselves as certain animals, and in that way, they escaped the violence and cruelty of mankind. Later, once they had secured dominion over the world, to show gratitude to the animals that had provided the means of their safety, they consecrated those whose forms they had assumed. They also demonstrated how these animals were to be nourished while living and how they were to be buried when dead.

<margin>The Second Cause.</margin>
The second cause: they say that the ancient Egyptians, who possessed no military doctrine and were frequently defeated in war by their neighbors, devised the idea of carrying certain standards for the soldiers to follow. Therefore, their leaders carried the figures of the animals they now worship into battle; because of this practice—knowing and maintaining the order under which each soldier served—they achieved victory. It therefore seemed right that gratitude be shown to these animals as the authors of their victory. It was established as a sacrilege <note>original: "nefas"; a divine sin or something forbidden by heaven</note> to kill any of the animals whose image had been carried, and ordained that they should instead be worshipped and honored.

<margin>The Third Cause.</margin>
A third cause is offered: the utility these animals bring to the human diet and way of life. The female cow gives birth to others who plow the earth, and she herself is not useless for plowing. Sheep give birth twice a year; they provide wool suited for various uses, and they offer us an abundance of milk and cheese. The dog is useful both for hunting and for guarding. For this reason, the god who is called Anubis among them...

These reasons did not satisfy Diodorus himself—a pagan who knew neither the knowledge of the true God nor the distinction between false deities, much less anything of <term>chemical truth</term> <note>original: "chymicæ veritatis"; here the author refers to the hidden secrets of alchemy, which he believes the Egyptians encoded in their religion</note>. These justifications seemed unworthy of the price of such great labor; likewise, they can be much less to our taste, as we are far differently instructed both in the true religion of God and in the study of **Alchemy**. Indeed, they are considered trifles and scarcely worthy of mention, being entirely foreign to all reason and experience.

Meanwhile, since the true causes—which would illuminate themselves by their own light—should not and could not be shared, whether by the ignorant commoners or the priests privy to the matter, some sort of form or pretext had to be fashioned. 
<margin>The Egyptians were most wise in ancient times.</margin>
When these stories appeared absurd to wiser men, they not unjustly mocked the stupidity of the Egyptians in worshipping their deities. Yet, no one can deny that the Egyptians were the first inventors and cultivators of many arts and sciences, and they have always been celebrated as men of the most prudent and subtle intellect. How, then, would they have fallen into such childish delusions regarding the worship of beasts more than other nations, unless some other, more secret cause—one not permitted to be revealed—lay beneath?

The priests, conscious of the truth and deterred by religious law and the threat of capital punishment, revealed nothing of these great **Secrets**. Others among the Egyptians, whether literate or unlearned, did not know even the slightest bit of the true cause; therefore, they could manifest nothing to others through their writing except fables and things fashioned for outward appearance. Thus, the more those seeking the true causes were deceived and led away from the mark, the more pleasing it was to the priests who were in the know. Since they were persuaded that God, the Creator of all, could be recognized and worshipped through His creatures, they were—by a mistaken imagination—not concerned that the common people were instructed otherwise in religion, for they foresaw that such a change would be most dangerous for themselves. But while the true reason for animal worship was kept hidden in silence, it was necessary for various false reasons to be produced, which would eventually contradict and destroy one another. For since the <term>chemical gods</term> <note>original: "dij chymici"; the author views Egyptian deities as personifications of alchemical processes or substances</note>—**Osiris**, **Isis**, **Mercury**, and **Vulcan**—feared the impiety of men, they did not wish to bestow their works upon them without discrimination. Therefore, they veiled and hid them under the figure and shape of various living creatures as if with a skin, so that they would not be recognized except by those who were "in the know" or guided by reason. For it was not safe to openly entrust the most hidden secrets of nature to Nilotic papyrus or animal skins <note>original: "membranis animantium"; parchment</note> through writing; instead, it seemed advisable to converse with one another using essential characters <note>original: "characteribus essentialibus"</note> taken from living beings. In this way, those listening or watching would not understand, while those who already possessed the knowledge would not remain ignorant.

<margin>*Two impulsive causes for worshipping the bull.* 1.</margin>
To which I answer: there are two primary motivating or impulsive causes for these introduced ceremonies and rituals. The first and chief was that thanks might be given daily by the knowing priests to God—the highest Creator and Giver of such great gifts—upon seeing this animal as a visible object and as if a sacrament and external symbol <note>original: "sacramento et symbolo externo"</note>. This would serve to remind them to direct the internal movements of the heart toward God. For just as the mind more easily retains what the hand has previously noted, so the hand more aptly expresses afterward what the mind has well premeditated.

<margin>2nd Cause.</margin>
The other and secondary cause concerns the common people. It was intended both to keep them in this duty and veneration of this animal—even though they remained ignorant of the true meaning—so they would comply with the laws, and also to prevent them from prying into the acts and writings of the Sages who handle the alchemical art. For if no external worship had been present in this matter, those Priests would have been proclaimed not as Priests, but as alchemical craftsmen, and everyone, out of curiosity, [would have pried] into their deeds and effects...

And just as the eggs of a hen produced without a rooster are useless, so the philosophical subject, or Apis, is of hardly any use without the image of the crescent moon.

Apis does not exceed his fourth year; when that year arrives, he is drowned, and another is sought in his place, to be nourished, worshipped, and extinguished in the same manner. <margin>
The origin of Egyptian superstition.
</margin>

This is the origin and root of the Egyptians' animalistic superstition in worshipping all kinds of animals and plants; it sprang from Apis and his hieroglyphics, sown and fixed into their minds. For while the ignorant person takes the sign for the thing signified—just as a dog, out of anger, snaps at a stone instead of the thrower—and clings to the external surface, he neglects the inner things which should be discerned by the intellect, not the eyes. While he chases the shadow, he loses the essence of the thing. Thus superstition was born from superstition and error from error, with the priests turning a blind eye for the reasons mentioned before. It was impossible for such an opinion, drunk in with mother's milk, to be rooted out afterward unless the truth was revealed—the truth for which these great and many things were ordained by the ancients—which was by no means permitted.

# Hieroglyphics, Book I

...as if Crocodiles living under water could better drive away an enemy than the Egyptians themselves, who are preoccupied and never secure under the tyranny of those crocodiles; since the Crocodile is more rapacious and cruel than all other predators, hostile to both Egyptians and foreigners, and feared in both the waters and the lands. That Menas <note>Referring to Pharaoh Menes/Aha, the legendary unifier of Egypt.</note> was carried by a Crocodile through the swamp of *Moeris* while his own dogs pursued him, and that he therefore commanded this beast to be worshipped as a God and built for it a city called Crocodilopolis—just as Lycopolis <note>City of the Wolf.</note> was for the Wolf and Leontopolis <note>City of the Lion.</note> for the Lion—is altogether incredible. It is more certain than certainty itself that this did not arise from the merit of the animals, but because of a secret physical <note>In this context, "physical" refers to *physica*, the study of natural philosophy or alchemy.</note> meaning not known to everyone. For this animal lives in both the waters and the lands, and alone among the quadrupeds it lays an egg; for which reason it truly expresses the philosophical egg; which, although it is imperfect, nevertheless has everything necessary for itself within it.

<margin>The Ibis.</margin>
The same reasoning applies to the Ibis, which was held to be most beneficial to Egypt for preying upon serpents. This bird was believed to be sacred to *Isis* and *Mercury* <note>The Roman name for Hermes/Thoth, the god of wisdom and writing.</note> because of secret natural gifts: both because by eating venomous things it rendered the air healthier and life safer for animals, and because it would heal itself from obstructions that blocked its bowels by the injection of a *Clyster* <note>The Ibis was famously credited by ancient authors like Pliny the Elder with inventing the enema (clyster) by using its long beak to inject water into its own body.</note>.

<margin>The Hawk.</margin>
They think the Hawk <note>original: *Accipiter*.</note> is sacred to *Osiris*, because it seems to be a solar bird, not only because of the sharpness of its eyes by which it prevails, but also its fiery nature ready for war; hence that line of *Ovid*:

->*We hate the hawk, because it always lives in arms.* <note>original: "Odimus accipitrem, quia semper vivit in armis." From Ovid's *The Art of Love*.</note><-

For by this martial force it calls other birds to prey, and converts them into its own blood.

<margin>The Eagle.</margin>
Before all these, however, they recognized the Eagle as the Queen of birds, and placed it among the sacred characters that the Egyptians call Hieroglyphics, for the same reasons we have reviewed before and will review later where the Eagle is mentioned. Besides these Hieroglyphic figures, innumerable others are found, such as in the Pyramids, the Table of Isis <note>The *Mensa Isiaca* or Bembine Tablet of Isis, a famous bronze tablet of Egyptian-style symbols popular among Renaissance occultists.</note>, and similar very ancient Egyptian works

The most true cause why the Gods are believed to rejoice or take delight in the forms of these animals was unknown to the common folk, except for what they might have thought (as we mentioned above under the first cause): that the Gods, terrified by the fear of the Giants, fled into Egypt and hid themselves there by assuming the shapes of various animals. Hence, *Ovid* in the 5th book of his *Metamorphoses* ascribes a specific animal to each of the Gods, under whose cover they lay hidden, in these verses:

<margin>Harpocrates</margin>
In addition to the figures of animals and other things used as Hieroglyphic characters, a statue of Harpocrates <note>The Greek interpretation of the Egyptian god Horus the Child, often associated with silence and secrets.</note> was seen in every one of the Egyptian temples. He was depicted in such a form that, with a finger pressed to his mouth, he suggested that silence must be kept, and with his other hand hiding his private parts, he indicated that lust must be loathed; and this was not without cause. For these things, insofar as they are the most hidden secrets of nature, are not to be instilled in everyone; and just as they are the most precious gifts of God, so they must not be dishonored by lust or luxury.

# Book 1: Egyptian-Greeks

...boys, following that custom brought over from Egypt. However, in these matters, <margin>Note.</margin> out of an ignorance of sacred scripture, he <note>The author is likely critiquing the Greek historian Diodorus Siculus, mentioned on the previous page, for his secular interpretation of biblical history.</note> traces the origin of circumcision among the Jews back to the Egyptians. In reality, the reverse is true; after **Abraham**—by the command of God Himself—passed this rite down to his descendants, many of them settled in Egypt at various times and undoubtedly spread the practice of circumcision there. 

In this departure of the Israelites from Egypt, a singular instance of the abundance of gold and silver riches among the Egyptians becomes apparent. Each of the Israelites was commanded by God to borrow vessels of gold and silver and carry them away. It appears there was both a vast quantity of these vessels and that they were held in relatively low esteem or value, given that rustic, enslaved foreigners—who were preparing to leave against the King’s will with no intention of returning—were able to obtain such items from their Egyptian neighbors. 

For beyond the fact that God held the will of the Egyptians in His hand and directed it, private individuals would not have been able to lend so much gold and silver if they did not possess a great deal of it themselves. If this was true for common people, what must we imagine for the Priests and Kings? Think of the vast treasures and wealth in metal they must have possessed, as it is written that they constructed their own storehouses or <term>treasuries</term> <note>Original Latin: *gazophylacia*. These were specifically designed chambers or vaults for storing temple wealth or royal tribute.</note> to safeguard their gold and silver—a fact that seems truly marvelous in that ancient age, though perhaps not in our own.

Glass, which could be called an artificial transparent stone and properly pertains to chemistry <term>chymia<note>In the 17th century, "chymia" encompassed both alchemy and what we now call chemistry, focused on the transformation of materials through fire and artifice.</note></term>, was known from the most ancient times to Egypt and its neighbor Ethiopia. Thus, the body of the deceased is seen through the glass, just as Herodotus <note>The 5th-century BC Greek historian often called the "Father of History."</note> writes; however, Ctesias of Cnidus <note>A Greek physician and historian who wrote about Persia and India.</note> disagrees with this. Instead, he says that hollow golden statues are made in which they place the dead, with glass placed around them. The result is that, when placed in higher positions, a golden image similar to the deceased is rendered to the onlookers through the surrounding glass. They affirm that these are the sepulchers of the wealthy; the middle class place silver images, and the poor use clay. Since glass is produced in great abundance in Ethiopia, everyone has access to it. We thought these things ought to be cited because the Ethiopians at one time ruled the Egyptians, and the Egyptians ruled a great part of the Ethiopians; this is so that no one, by imagining a lack of vessels required for the use of chemistry at that time, might conclude otherwise than the reality of the matter.

Besides the aforementioned *Osiris*, *Isis*, and *Horus*, the most ancient Egyptians also used the names of other Gods, especially twelve: namely *Jupiter*, *Neptune*, *Mars*, *Mercury*, *Vulcan*, *Apollo*, *Juno*, *Vesta*, *Ceres*, *Venus*, *Diana*, and *Minerva*. Six of these are of the masculine and six of the feminine sex; these were believed to be the Great Gods of the great nations, and were later transferred to the Greeks, and from them to the Romans. For as Natalis <note>Natalis Comes (1520–1582) was a famous mythographer whose handbook *Mythologiae* was the standard Renaissance resource for interpreting ancient myths.</note> testifies, for other [minor] gods, images were made of wood or clay, and they were not sculpted from gold, silver, or ivory unless they were "Great Gods," whereas those of the common deities were made from any material in ancient times. Regarding these, *Herodotus* writes in *Euterpe* <note>The second book of Herodotus's *Histories*, which focuses almost entirely on Egypt.</note>: *The Egyptians were the first to conceive the names of the twelve Gods, and the Greeks took them from them; they were also the first to erect altars, images, and Temples to the Gods.* Furthermore, that the Greeks—and specifically which ones among them—
<margin>The Greeks received doctrines from the Egyptians.</margin>
were the first to cross over to the Egyptians and bring their sacred rites back to Greece, we shall demonstrate by the words of *Diodorus* <note>Diodorus Siculus, a 1st-century BCE historian who argued that Greek culture was essentially a "colony" of Egyptian wisdom.</note> himself. Here in Book 2, Chapter 6, he says: *We shall now recount which Greeks, endowed with wisdom and learning, crossed into Egypt in ancient times to learn their laws and doctrine. Their Priests write that it is recorded in the sacred books that first there crossed over to the Egyptians Orpheus, Musaeus, Melampus, Daedalus, the Poet Homer, and the Spartan Lycurgus; afterwards Solon the Athenian, Plato the Philosopher, and Pythagoras of Samos; also Eudoxus the Mathematician, Democritus of Abdera, and Inopides of Chios.*
<margin>Which Greeks first crossed into Egypt.</margin>
Indeed, traces of all of them are shown: images of some, locations of others, named either after them or after the doctrine which they followed. Certainly, in Egypt they learned everything that made them famous among the Greeks. For they say that *Orpheus* brought many hymns of the Gods, the mysteries <note>original: *orgia*; refers to secret ritual celebrations or rites, often involving ecstatic worship.</note>, and the poetic description of the underworld; truly the ceremonies of *Osiris* and *Dionysus* <note>The Greek god of wine; the author is identifying him as the Greek version of the Egyptian Osiris.</note> are the same, and the names of *Isis* and *Ceres* <note>The Roman goddess of agriculture, equivalent to the Greek Demeter.</note> are similar...

<margin>When the Egyptian rites were transferred to the Greeks.</margin>
When this happened, however, and with what primary intention, is easy to discern: namely, at that time when it was granted to the Greeks to seek out and enter Egypt without danger of death. This occurred, as we mentioned before, in the age of King **Psammetichus** <note>Psammetichus I (reigned 664–610 BC), the pharaoh who famously opened Egypt to Greek trade and settlement.</note>, one of the twelve leaders, who first admitted foreigners to himself. ### Book 2. Of the Egyptian-Greeks.

...to slaughter the triumphant leader. <margin>*The primary intention of the most ancient poets.*</margin> However, if we wish to inquire more subtly into the intention of **Orpheus** and other ancient poets, we will find in reality that they did not look primarily toward those divine cults or ceremonies. Instead, they looked toward other most secret things <note>original: "arcanissima"; referring to the Hermetic or Alchemical secrets believed to be hidden in ancient myth.</note> hidden beneath them, so that these matters would not become known to the common people, yet would provide a cause for investigation to others who are wiser. Although this has been indicated nowhere by any specific writer (because the matter remained hidden and was not even expressed by name), it can nevertheless be most clearly shown by us from various signs and arguments collected here and there, as will appear in what follows. 

Even without considering these, this single reason would suffice for the intelligent: namely, if the Egyptians understood something else by their sacred rites and ceremonies involving **Osiris**, **Isis**, **Mercury**, **Vulcan**, **Apis**, and certain animals, other than the objects themselves obvious to the eyes, and hid the kernel of truth beneath them like husks <note>The author uses the metaphor of "corticibus" (husks/bark) and "nucleum" (kernel) to describe the relationship between a myth's surface story and its hidden philosophical meaning.</note>; so too the Greeks would not have been concerned with the coverings unless they also recognized a "body" to be covered beneath them. We have already sufficiently investigated and explained what that "body" was under the Egyptian **Hieroglyphics**. 

Hence, it is not likely that those ancient poets, out of innate malice or for the sake of mockery, attributed so many adulteries, homicides, incests, and crimes to their gods to mock either gods or men, or to propagate such enormous vices by the examples of the gods (for then they would have been the most wicked of all two-legged creatures). Rather, they did so to demonstrate that those gods are nothing but fictional and imaginary symbols and **Emblems** of an art hidden from the common people, but known to themselves—referring one thing to the eye and another to the mind. Lest they seem to bring forward empty names void of substance, they ascribed to each of those fictional gods individual, quasi-divine offices and various powers of mother **Nature** <note>The author suggests the gods represent different physical forces or chemical properties of the natural world.</note>, and nevertheless professed **One God** in all of them. Therefore, if these Gods were taken literally—as has been the custom among the Pagans until now—water and fire, the Nymphs and Vulcan, war and peace, Mars and Venus, are in no way "one." If one refers these to the One God of the universe, perhaps such opposing qualities could be excused in Him, if they are understood as His power diffused through all Created things. However, I fear that this would be done too improperly and impiously, by confusing the Creator with the created, the Eternal with the changeable, and Spirit with bodies. Therefore, it seems entirely necessary that those gods, so varied and diverse, and so different from one another, should be understood and explained through another subject to which they all equally apply. This is the very same subject in which the Egyptian gods (the ancestors of the Greeks)—**Osiris**, **Isis**, **Typhon**, **Mercury**, and others—are declared to lie hidden. ### Book 2: Of the Egypto-Greeks.

...tales, which they call poetic; these we shall take up to be illustrated by us in this second book and those following, so that the fictional gods of the nations may be restored to their true origin, and likewise true <term>Chemistry<note>original: "Chymia." These are people who receive, embrace, and kiss the genealogies and deeds of gods, goddesses, and heroes as if they were certain, true, and irrefutable; indeed, they cherish and admire them as if they were the "Brain of Jupiter" <note>A proverbial expression for something exquisitely delightful or a supreme delicacy.</note>, forgetting meanwhile that they are Christians and that truth is one and simple. For these sciences and persons shall receive from us not an obscuring of their name, but rather an illustration. If what we say is not to their taste, we hope they will not hurl accusations at us, but rather realize that the shadows have been stripped from their minds. We shall strive to provide this for them, provided they do not do the same to us. I do not think a blind man can give any true judgment concerning colors; therefore, when a dispute regarding these things arises, it would be more well-advised for him to indulge in silence rather than in ridiculous talk. Hence, if anyone wishes to notice these secrets, it is required that he have them well-understood before he brandishes his Censorship. As to how far we have penetrated into these matters with both mind and hand, it is not for us to boast; rather, we are bound to offer here a sacrifice of praise to God (of which this work is a specimen), which may also serve the benefit of men of good will.

Since, however, it would be a work of a great volume to unwrap such great and varied entanglements according to the dignity and breadth of the material—to re-examine what has been woven through so many centuries and writings, and to polish it to the finest detail <note>original: "ad unguem," literally "to the fingernail," a Latin idiom for perfect craftsmanship.</note>—and the work would therefore suffer under its own weight; for that reason, we have selected only the principal and more remarkable of all the allegorical fictions of the *Poets* and the fabulous narrations concerning the Gods and heroes for our treatment. We have done so not with a sharp or copious style, as others are accustomed, but in a common one, adapted more to the matter than to the words, and succinct. Thus, in this second book, we treat the Expedition of the Greeks under the leadership of Jason.

[Pelias], the son of Neptune born from Tyro, daughter of Salmoneus (who had been raised by Salmoneus’s brother Cretheus), had seized Iolcus after the death of Cretheus, its founder. However, the more Jason excelled in every virtue, the less he was able to earn the love of Pelias, for he was constantly watched by the king with suspicion. Therefore, so that Pelias might expose Jason to present dangers and even to death under an honorable pretext, he commanded him to bring back the Golden Fleece—famous among the Colchians—to him, overcoming great perils with the singular fortitude of spirit that befitted such a youth. Although this seemed a harsh command and an arduous task to perform, it nevertheless gave Jason courage, because he was bound to carry it out not from his own arrogance, but by the command of another, whom it would be a sin to disobey. Third, a certain clear water that would very easily extinguish the fire of the bulls. Fourth, an image of the Moon and the Sun crafted in a peculiar way; if he wore this around his neck, whatever he attempted in this labor would succeed perfectly. When he had cut off its head with a sword, he extracted its teeth from there. Next, he proceeded to tame the bulls; but they soon pursued Jason, attacking with their horns and drenching him in a fiery rain. He, retreating somewhat behind a tree, sprinkled the clearest water into their jaws; whence they stood still immediately, as if stunned and tamed. Therefore, with the yoke fitted to their necks, he began to turn the earth with a plow and cast the dragon's teeth as seed. But as this seed was covered under the earth, behold, armed men soon appeared, born according to the number of the teeth, who, when they rushed at Jason, he—as he had learned from Medea—withdrawing himself slightly from their sight, struck one of them with a stone from a distance. 

<margin>One of the earth-born struck by a stone.</margin>This man, while he thought he was being beaten by the man next to him, pierced the other with a drawn blade; and as one after another avenged his death, a mutual battle overwhelmed them all to a man. When these were slain, since nothing more remained that could hinder the taking of the Golden Fleece, having finally gained possession of it, he returned safely to his homeland together with Medea. And this is the succinct narrative of the deed performed by Jason, which, after Orpheus, both Apollonius <note>Apollonius of Rhodes, author of the Greek epic *Argonautica*.</note> among the Greeks and Valerius Flaccus <note>Gaius Valerius Flaccus, author of the Latin epic *Argonautica*.</note> among the Romans recorded, besides countless others whom we do not cite. Others add more circumstances regarding the departure and return, all of which it is not the place here to attach, nor is it worth the effort. How Medea then tore her brother Absyrtus into pieces near the Absyrtian islands, and restored Aeson—Jason's aged father—to youth, and performed other wonders, and finally how Jason died, crushed while sleeping under the ship *Argo*, is found noted among various authors. Likewise, how Phryxus (from whom Phrygia is said by some to be named...
