### Book 3. Of the Egyptian-Greeks.

...they receive what was performed by the following Jovial <note>The "Jovial" age refers to the era of Jupiter, which succeeded the reign of Saturn.</note> age: **Natalis Comes**, dealing with **Saturn**, poorly receives the judgments of those treating chemical matters regarding this planet:

<margin>He fights like a blindfolded gladiator.</margin> <note>original: "Andabata pugnat," an ancient Roman term for a gladiator who fought without sight; here used as an idiom for someone attacking a subject they do not understand.</note>

*“Moreover,”* he says, *“since individual metals are attributed to individual planets due to a certain similarity, the **torturers of metals**, or alchemical craftsmen, have twisted almost this entire fable toward their own art, although they profess that they wish to imitate the Platonists **Geber**, **Hermes**, and **Raymond** <note>Reference to the foundational alchemical figures Jabir ibn Hayyan, Hermes Trismegistus, and Ramon Llull.</note>: For they say it was a fiction of the ancients that **Jupiter** cut off the genital parts of **Saturn** with a sharp scythe and cast them into the sea, from which, and from the foam, **Venus** was born; because Saturn is a certain salt, the father of Jupiter—that is, of prepared salt—which is made from him when prepared. But since, when Jupiter exists in a glass vessel, he is dissolved into very sharp and thin water due to the force of fire, which is also taken from Jupiter himself, since he brings the virile parts with him, cutting into and separating the innermost sulfur lying hidden in the salt, which falls back into the vessel placed to receive them; therefore they say the virile parts were cut off from Saturn, and since the salt falls into the water as if into a sea, from that salt and sulfur, **Venus** is born.”* For the torturers of metals endeavor to devise both these and other similar arts by which they might be able to transform metals into other forms, terrified by the most foul form of poverty, and always having in mind that sentiment of the most witty poet **Timocles**, who says: *“Money is blood and spirit to mortals; he who has no abundance of it wanders among the living like the shadows of the dead.”* 

<margin>A fair response to the slanders.</margin>

But kind words, I pray, **Comes**; does the Saturnine star so haunt you that you thus provoke the whole alchemical art and think it a dream because of the interpretation of one or two fables that do not please your palate? Let us grant that he who wrote thus about Saturn (perhaps you mean the Italian **Bracesco** <note>Giovanni Bracesco, a 16th-century author who wrote "The Exposition of Geber," interpreting myths as alchemical recipes.</note>) applied those things poorly; is there therefore no truth in alchemy? Meanwhile, he understood those things—which you twist toward morals—to relate instead to the secrets of alchemy and nature. What if alchemy is true even against your prejudice, and beyond your grasp? Because you judge otherwise or do not understand it, will you therefore make it false? You will not, I pray. My discourse is not about the “torturers of metals,” but about the art...

### Book 3 of the Hieroglyphics

...chemical **substance**, which perfects the **Golden Medicine** <note>Also known as the Universal Medicine or the Elixir of Life.</note>, even if it does not manufacture literal gold, nor does it strive for anything contrary to nature. You may brand those men as forgers with a mark of shame if you wish—those who are not seekers of truth and have no need of your judgment—but what if a man treating chemical matters perfects a Medicine with which he helps the sick? Shall he not be worthy of his reward or prize? Is it not fitting for him to escape poverty by this very means? 

It is no wonder, therefore, if those whom you call "torturers of metals" do this in their own legitimate way. It is well established that some of them (I speak of the true ones) have elicited more truth from metals than you, perhaps, have extorted from fables—to say nothing of their practical utility. **Geber**, **Hermes**, and **Raymond** <note>Jabir ibn Hayyan, Hermes Trismegistus, and Ramon Llull, foundational figures in the alchemical tradition.</note> were not merely "Platonists" <note>The author argues they were practical experimentalists, not just abstract philosophers.</note>; let him who is able imitate them in work, rather than in outward show. 

We do not accept **Saturn** as a substitute for sulfur or salt, yet we assert that his color <note>The "blacker than black" stage of the alchemical process, known as the *nigredo*.</note> appears before the **philosophical sulfur** is truly made. What is understood by his genitals we shall discuss more broadly under the exposition of **Venus**. 

Certain ancient writers claim that **Saturn** reigned in **Egypt** and took his sister **Rhea** in marriage, from whom **Jupiter** and **Juno** were born; from these, five children were born. They attributed a **key** and a **staff** to Saturn, perhaps because he shared a connection with the two-faced **Janus**, who is the gate of the year, and with whom Saturn is said to have lived. 

<margin>A secret cause.</margin>
What advantages Saturn discovered, and why he is called the "light of human life," has not been sufficiently made known, unless the cause is a secret one. Why were his festivals <note>The Saturnalia.</note> celebrated among the Romans with such a ridiculous rite, where masters served their servants, and no one used anything but the 

<margin>Aulus Gellius, Book 18, Chapter 2.</margin>
utmost freedom of speech? For this highest Planet <note>In the ancient geocentric model, Saturn was the outermost and "highest" of the seven planets.</note> undergoes a conjunction with the lowest and the middle. 

So says **Avicenna** <note>Ibn Sina (c. 980–1037), a Persian physician and philosopher whose works were central to medieval alchemy.</note> in *On the Soul*, discourse 1, chapter 2: 

*“And just as the sun is more powerful, giving its strength even unto Saturn, and downward even unto the moon, so gold is more precious than all others; and because all celestial things are mixed with terrestrial things, they thus send their strength from above to below. For it was the strength of the earthly things to ascend upward, and the strength of the higher things to descend downward. And just as it cannot happen that Saturn does not run with the sun in the same sign, so it cannot happen that this...”*

*...that this mastery <note>term: magisterium; the "Mastery" or "Great Work," referring to the successful completion of the alchemical process to create the Philosopher's Stone or Universal Medicine.</note> does not extract gold from lead: But understand what we wish to say—once you have the reasoning, it is impossible that the Mastery does not exist.* The same is affirmed by the author of the *Rose Garden* <note>original: "Rosarius"; referring to the *Rosarium Philosophorum*, a famous 16th-century alchemical treatise.</note> and Emiganus in the *Crowd* <note>original: "in turba"; referring to the *Turba Philosophorum* (Assembly of the Philosophers), one of the oldest Latin alchemical texts.</note>: they state that the sun gives its light upward as far as the moon, and then it looks back upon all things, both those above and those below. This is related by **Hermes Trismegistus** regarding the three wise men famous in his time—**Caelus** <note>The personification of the Sky.</note>, **Saturn**, and **Mercury**. This convicts all the Pagans of falsehood: for how could these three be said to have lived at the same time unless it were told allegorically? Enough has been said of these. This is the summary of the story: He is said to have been born at Thebes in Arcadia among the Messenians, snatched from **Saturn** in Boeotia, and handed over to the **Corybantes** in Crete to be raised. These attendants, by means of feigned sacrifices amidst the din of cymbals and drums, concealed the crying of the infant. He had as nurses **Adrastea** and **Ida**, the daughters of **Melisseus** and sisters of the **Curetes** or **Dactyls**. When **Jupiter** had reached adulthood and **Titan** <note>Saturn's brother.</note> realized that the sons of **Saturn** were being raised in secret, contrary to the oath and the laws, he and his sons, the **Titans**, burned with rage; they seized **Saturn** and **Ops** <note>Saturn's wife, the goddess of abundance.</note>, threw them into chains, and cast them into prison. **Jupiter**, however, defeated the **Titans** in war and freed his father. After this, **Saturn** prepared an ambush for **Jupiter**, fearing what might happen to him at his son's hands. Then **Jupiter** cast his father down from the kingdom, bound him with a woolen cord, and thrust him into **Tartarus** <note>The deep abyss used as a dungeon of torment.</note>. ...nourished your fire, together with Virginity, as histories testify: how **Jupiter** obtained the love of **Juno**, as well as marriage, is a thing most absurd if taken literally; but if the hidden sense is regarded, perhaps it will represent a harmony with the nature of the bird. The Cuckoo—in whose nest another small bird places her eggs—is devoured by the hatched chick as a reward for its nursing, a detestable mark of ingratitude. To attribute such things to Gods and Goddesses would seem foreign to such a very mad people; however, allegories of this kind excuse it, perhaps because the mother is devoured by the son in the **Philosophical Mastery** <term>Philosophical Mastery: The "Great Work" or process of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</term> and the sister by the brother. 

Thus **Raymond Lull** <note>A 13th-century philosopher and reputed alchemist.</note> says in his *Theory of the Testament*, chapter 87: *Accept a vile thing and make it embrace its parents, until they completely burst, and are as if dead.* And in the same work: *Quicksilver* <note>original: "Argentum vivum"</note> *is the cause of its own death, because it kills its very self, and afterwards kills its father and mother, and extracts their souls from their bodies, and drinks up all their moisture.* 

**Juno** was held to be the Goddess of Riches, because her golden bond was cast on her hands, and the Goddess herself was hung high by her feet by **Jupiter**. Since the active and passive parts—the fixed and the volatile—are **Jupiter** and **Juno**, she is sometimes suspended in the air because of her volatility, while she ascends and adheres to the superior part <note>This describes the process of sublimation, where matter rises as vapor to the top of the flask.</note>. Watery portions are attributed to the Nymphs; and the **Peacock** reflects various colors, which occur by reason of the volatile matter; for while the whole remains fixed, there is one unchangeable color.

**Pluto** also is the God of wealth, because riches are sought from the lower places of the earth, over which he presides. To him the Bull is sacred—that is, the Egyptian **Apis**—because they are of one intention. He inhabits the **Pyrenean mountains**, because those were the first places from which metals were sought in Europe by the Phoenicians, as said before. From there also **Hercules** drove away his cattle. To him **Cerberus** was the guardian, who was three-headed, and **Keys** were his emblem, because without his key nothing can be obtained <note>The "key" often refers to the specific solvent or secret process required to open or dissolve the "fixed" matter.</note>. <margin>Neptune.</margin>
**Neptune**, the third son of **Saturn**, was allotted by authority the sea and the islands of the sea. He had **Amphitrite** as his wife, by whom and by various mistresses he fathered a great number of sons: **Phoenix**, a son from **Libya**; and **Ion**, a son from **Pyrene**;

<margin>Phoenix. Io.</margin>
whom **Jupiter** compressed <note>A common euphemism in Latin for sexual union.</note> within a cloud so that he might remain hidden; but when **Juno** intervened, he changed her into a white cow. She was then worshiped by the Egyptians under the name of **Isis**. From this, the statue of **Isis** was fashioned with horns, sometimes called the moon, sometimes the earth. However, that the Cow is the hieroglyphic image of **Isis** and **Juno**, just as the Bull is of **Osiris** and **Pluto**, has been sufficiently declared above. **Neptune**, together with **Apollo**, built the walls of Troy. The sons of this same **Neptune** are:

<margin>Proteus.</margin>
**Proteus**, by the nymph **Phoenix**; and **Triton**, by **Amphitrite**. The sons of **Proteus** were **Tmylus** and **Telegonus**, who were killed by **Hercules** because they would murder their guests; and a daughter, **Idothea**, who taught **Menelaus** how **Proteus**, her father, was to be captured,

<margin>Triton.</margin>
as **Homer** relates in the 4th book of the *Odyssey*. **Triton** is the herald and trumpeter of **Neptune**. His daughter **Tritia**, a virgin priestess of **Minerva**, was compressed by **Mars** and gave birth to **Melanippus**. **Triton** was the cause of victory for **Jupiter** while he was waging war against the Giants, when he produced an unheard-of sound with a found conch shell, by which they were turned to flight. The upper part of his body as far as the navel was that of a man, the lower part reaching to the tail was that of a dolphin;

Many thousands of temples were established and dedicated, and countless myriads of wanton women were consecrated to her service—that is, to lust. And since Venus was once accepted as a Goddess so benevolent to the human race, no one was found who declared war on her, or who did not most zealously study her cult and enslave themselves to it. To revere **Mars** as a God and to bestow honor upon him seemed somewhat contrary to human nature, because he was believed to delight in the shedding of blood and in death; on the other hand, to acknowledge the Goddess **Venus** and to show her reverence through pleasures was judged to be lovely and pleasant to every kind of person.

<margin>
Venus was accepted as a goddess because she is a friend to nature.
</margin>

Yet the blindness of the human mind must be deplored in these matters as in others, for it could hardly distinguish the lawful from the unlawful, or good from evil. **Venus** was not introduced by the *Egyptians* and the most ancient *Greeks* for the sake of lust, but as the daughter of **Saturn** (whose sister is **Truth**, hidden in a deep cave). She was one who was most beautiful and who would ignite the fire in our subject—that is, the love and appetite for propagating itself. This was the occasion for all idolatry and the cult of Venus. [one must] understand [her] as animal lust or the pleasure and desire for mating—as certain mythologists crudely explain the stories of Venus—nor as that celestial star which they call Venus, Hesperus, or Lucifer <note>The morning and evening star (Planet Venus).</note>, the precursor or attendant of the sun; nor as that well-known common metal which the common sort of chemists also call by this name <note>Copper, which is traditionally associated with the planet Venus in alchemy.</note>; but rather as a certain **philosophical subject**, without which nothing can be achieved. > *I generate light, and darkness is not of my nature; and were my metal not dry, all bodies would have need of me; for I liquefy them, and I wipe away their rust, and I extract their substance. Therefore, nothing is better or more venerable than me and my invincible brother. But the King, the ruler, testifying for his brothers, says: I am crowned and adorned with a diadem, and I am clothed in your kingdom, and I bring joy to hearts; and I, bound by bonds to the breast of my mother and to her substance, cause my own substance to hold together and rest; I compose the invisible from the visible, then the hidden shall appear, and everything which the philosophers have hidden shall be birthed from us.*

So says **Flamel**, quoting **Democritus**:
> *Therefore, drawing out the body of the brass <note>original: "Aeris". In alchemy, this often refers to the "Aes Hermetis" or the crude metallic body before purification.</note> as much as is appropriate, make it like a certain long tongue. Afterward, placing it over the coals, stir it into the very fire <note>original: "vulcanum," referring to Vulcan, the god of fire.</note>, illuminating it now with rock salt, now with Attic ochre <note>A yellow earth pigment used in antiquity.</note> continuously; by adorning the shoulder and breast of the Paphian <note>An epithet for Venus, referring to her temple at Paphos.</note> either alternately or steadily, she will clearly become more beautiful, and casting off her grey-blue color, she will appear entirely golden.*

When **Paris** had perhaps seen such a Venus, he preferred her over **Juno** and **Pallas**. And in the same place:
> *Venus, like a human, has a soul and a body. It is necessary, therefore, to strip the matter of its body, so that the remaining staining spirit <note>term: "spiritu tingente" — a substance capable of "tinging" or transforming base metals into gold.</note> may be adapted to the perfection of whatever is sought. What is Venus? That which is the material body of a human. The soul is indeed the subtle part within her, which comes forth into the light through guided treatment—that is, the spirit having the power of staining. But the body is heavy, material, and earthy, which has its own shadow, which must be stripped away by the fiery medicine.*

These words from him are sufficient.

<margin>
*Why multiple Venuses and gods of the same name are counted.*
</margin>
**Cicero**, in the third book of *On the Nature of the Gods*, following **Varro** and **Orpheus** the Roman (or the ethnic theologian), brings forth several Venuses, as he was accustomed to do regarding all other gods, goddesses, and heroes. For since these personae are at least truly hieroglyphic and fashioned according to the intention of those who recognized them...

# Hieroglyphics, Book 3

<page-num>114</page-num>
<header>Hieroglyphics, Book 3</header>

...they understood these things hiddenly; hence it happened that a god, goddess, hero, or heroine are said to be born from various parents, places, times, and circumstances, as is clear in almost all cases. And therefore, so that fable or falsehood would not seem to be present in accepted religion, a distinction was found as a remedy, by which even the most diverse accounts could be reconciled. In this way, I say, **Cicero** in the mentioned place <note>original: "dicto loco"—referring to Cicero's *De Natura Deorum* (On the Nature of the Gods), Book 3.</note> affirms there were three **Venuses**, diverse as to their origin: the first born from **Heaven** and **Day**, whose shrine stands at **Elis**; the second from foam, from whom and **Mercury** the second **Cupid** was born; the third procreated from **Jupiter** and **Dione**, who married **Vulcan**. We know that **Venus** was neither a goddess nor a human, but a personage introduced among the **Egyptians**, as if for the stage, to declare the things hidden under those names. Therefore, the older writers handed down that she was born from **Jupiter** and **Juno**, together with **Osiris**, **Isis**, **Typhon**, and **Apollo**. Whether therefore **Venus** is said to be born from **Saturn**, or **Jupiter**, or **Heaven**, or elsewhere, the thing itself is nonetheless one, and not many, despite how the wiser among the **Pagans** <note>original: "Ethnicis".</note> have raved. If authors agree on the thing itself, they do not care about the names; for they say names exist for the sake of things, and not things for the sake of names. These [names] take the place of clothing; those things are the bodies of living beings. The lover loves the "stuffing" of the clothes, says the **Comic poet**, <note>Likely referring to a line from the Roman playwrights Plautus or Terence.</note> not the clothes themselves. So also the philosophers admire and respect the "stuffing" of names, not the names themselves—that is, the things alone. Nor because of this will whatever is said about the gods cease to be a fable, though **Cicero** distinguishes well between persons, things, and times; cautiously enough, indeed, but not truly. For his distinctions concern non-entities and things manifestly false: Was **Venus** born from **Heaven** and **Day**? Did **Heaven** lie with **Day**, as with the previously mentioned **Earth**? O Physicians, pierce the middle vein! <note>original: "Medici mediã pertundite venam"—A classical medical reference suggesting the patient is so insane they need immediate bloodletting to cool their frenzy.</note> **Cicero** is insane with too much wisdom. 

<margin>
The Pagans are insane in divine matters when they seem to themselves to be wise.
</margin>

Thus he makes three **Jupiters**, of whom the first and second were born in **Arcadia**, this one from **Heaven**, that one from **Aether** as father; he says the third was the **Cretan**, who had **Saturn** as a father. From the first, **Proserpina** and **Liber** <note>Also known as Bacchus or Dionysus.</note> were born; from the most ancient **Jupiter**, King of **Athens**, and **Proserpina**, the **Dioscuri** <note>The twins Castor and Pollux.</note> were born. Likewise he makes five **Mercuries**, several **Apollos**, and several **Cupids**...

<page-num>115</page-num>

...[wise men] <note>completing the word "Sapientes" from the previous page</note>, Bacchuses, Herculeses, Suns, Moons, or Dianas, as we shall see in their proper places. Let the mythologists <note>original: "Mythologi"—those who interpret myths</note> also forgive me for not portraying **Venus** as a symbol of luxury or lust, as has pleased the whole world until now. For if the discussion is about the primary origin and the truth of the matter, I believe we must think and speak according to the reality; but if it concerns accepted custom, I do not think we should depart from it without a clear reason. 

Doctors know that functions in the bodies of animals, and especially humans, are varied: natural, vital, and animal functions. These are further distinguished into sensory and motor functions, Intellect and Will, and there are many differences among each of these, along with various organs and locations. Among the natural functions, one is called the **generative function**, which is located in the members dedicated to procreation; it is this function that the mythologists explain through the goddess **Venus**. 

But if this is allowed, where are the others dedicated to other functions? Where are **Salacia** <note>Goddess of the sea's surface</note>, **Venilia** <note>Goddess of the tides or hope</note>, **Cinxia** <note>Goddess of the bridal girdle</note>, **Prema** <note>Goddess of physical pressure</note>, **Virginensis** <note>Goddess of the marriage chamber</note>, **Partunda** <note>Goddess of intimacy</note>, **Lucina** <note>Goddess of light and childbirth</note>, **Rumina** <note>Goddess of breastfeeding</note>, **Cunina** <note>Goddess of the cradle</note>, **Edulica** <note>Goddess of eating</note>, **Potina** <note>Goddess of drinking</note>, and who could count them all? We have already recounted that **Venus** was the lover of **Adonis**; whose mother she was, and by whom she conceived children, we shall say in what follows. 

<margin>Truth, the daughter of Time. Children of Jupiter.</margin> 

Enough regarding the children of **Saturn**, except that we are to deal with the unique **Truth** <note>original: "Veritas"</note>, who must be searched for throughout this entire treatise and who is called the **Daughter of Time**. Now we return to **Jupiter** and **Juno**: **Jupiter** had first married **Metis** <note>the personification of wisdom and cunning</note>, the daughter of **Ocean**. She later gave **Saturn** a potion to drink, by which he vomited up first the **Stone**, and then the children he had previously swallowed. 

<margin>Pallas without a mother. 1st daughter of Jupiter.</margin>

But when she became pregnant, **Jupiter** (whether out of love or hatred, it is unknown) swallowed her. From this "food" he soon became pregnant himself and gave birth from his head to **Pallas** <note>Athena</note>, fully armed. Afterward he married **Themis** <note>Divine Law</note>, and thirdly **Juno**, whom he kept as his wife. Others say that **Thetis** <note>a sea nymph</note>, after turning into various forms, was finally compressed <note>forced into union</note> by **Jupiter**. When she was pregnant, **Jupiter** heard a prophecy that one would be born from her who would seize the empire of Heaven, so he absorbed her; therefore, he himself later gave birth to **Pallas** near the river **Triton**. 

She was called **Tritonia** for that reason, or because she was raised by **Triton**. Thus, **Pallas** was born from the brain of **Jupiter** without a mother, with **Vulcan** providing a way for her with his axe. As **Homer** says...

Others write that Pallas was placed in the care of **Dionysus** when he was being raised in Nysa by **Ammon**, in order to avoid the traps of **Rhea**; these authors identify Ammon as either Saturn or **Jupiter**. 

Several authors disagree on the reasoning behind her name. Some think she was named Pallas because she brought the palpitating heart <note>original: "cor palpitans"</note> of Dionysus (who had been torn apart by the Titans) to Jupiter; others because she throws javelins <note>original: "iacula mittat"</note>; and others because she killed the giant **Pallas** with a javelin. From wherever the name arises, she is called Pallas, **Tritonia**, and Minerva interchangeably. It is believed she remained a perpetual virgin. She struck **Tiresias** blind because he had seen her naked while she was bathing in the **Hippocrene** spring on Mount Helicon. **Vulcan**, too, wishing to force himself upon her, was frustrated in his hope, as we mentioned earlier. The matter of the **Palladium** <note>The sacred statue of Pallas that protected Troy</note> will be dealt with below under the requirements of Troy.

What the ancients understood by this goddess is now easily perceived by anyone. Indeed, we believe that nothing else is denoted by Pallas being born from the brain of Jupiter except the **wisdom of a sharp mind and a clear intellect**. Without her, nothing is accomplished, neither in arduous business affairs nor in the **philosophical mastery** <note>original: "magisterio philosophico"—a term often referring to the "Great Work" of alchemy or high philosophy</note>, which is why it is called the "work of the wise." This contemplation of secrets designated by Pallas must not be prostituted to the common crowd, but must be hidden under the veils of philosophy, as the philosophers warn in many places with oaths and imprecations. 

Hence, Tiresias is undoubtedly imagined as blinded because he saw Pallas naked—just as **Actaeon** was turned into a stag for seeing **Diana**. Furthermore, when **Juno** heard of the monstrous birth of Pallas from the brain of her husband, she is said to have struck the earth in anger with

**Venus**, the most beautiful of women, tender and most luxurious, had married **Vulcan**, a husband who was deformed, lame, and a common laborer. Thus **Mars** coupled with her secretly, but having been betrayed by the Sun, he was bound by Vulcan with invisible, unbreakable chains, so that they provided laughter and sport for the gods looking on. Pagan poets and writers take and interpret Mars as the god of war, and as representing anger, vengeance, bile, and fury. However, the most ancient thinkers looked toward a certain fiery, burning force produced by Jupiter, which does not fear to endure the attacks and battles of fire, and is as if it possessed an invulnerable body. If our **Venus** should lie with this **Mars** in a fit bed, and be bound by **Vulcan** with a net of bronze or steel, there will be born from them a most beautiful daughter <margin>*By others she is called Hermione, for whom Vulcan fashioned a beautiful but deadly necklace.*</margin> called **Harmonia**; that is, one harmoniously composed and perfect in every part <note>original: "omnibus numeris absoluta"</note>, who in ancient times was said to be a guardian deity. At her wedding, all the gods and goddesses were present with their gifts and wedding songs <note>term: epithalamia — songs performed at the doorway of a bridal chamber</note>, which are recounted by various poets. She married **Cadmus**, whom we mentioned above, the son of **Agenor**, king of the Phoenicians. The **Dragon**, who killed Cadmus's companions when they were ordered to fetch water, is himself said by some to be the son of Mars and Venus; thus he was the uncle of Harmonia. After many calamities which Cadmus is said to have endured, he is imagined to have been turned into a dragon along with his wife Harmonia. Thus, the death of nearly all hieroglyphic gods or heroes corresponds to their origin, so that it may be seen they are not merely fables. For **Harmonia**, born of Mars and Venus, is that **Golden Medicine** <note>A term for the Philosopher's Stone or the final alchemical goal</note> produced for the first time by long labor. If she is joined to Cadmus (from whom our <term>Cadmia</term> <note>Likely referring to zinc oxide or cobalt ores used in alchemy</note> is named), then all the gods are present with their gifts...

But I am incorruptible and the son of the **Sun**, and the smallest part of my substance is my whole container, nor can anything corruptible be found in me; and yet these men want to multiply me and my substance out of corruptible things; how can they create sons like me without my consent and counsel? <margin>*Gargittius, envious of Hercules.*</margin> I do not know; but let him have his own scoffs, for *he has the eyes of a dog* <note>original Greek: "κύτον οὐμματ ἔχειν" (likely a corruption of κυνὸς ὄμματ' ἔχειν). He thinks that the best medicines can be prepared without the service of fire, in which he is mistaken. For the best medicines require the best element, which is **fire**, as it is closest to spirituality and simplicity, and without it neither nature nor art can operate.

# Book 3 of the Hieroglyphics

<page-num>120</page-num>

->...cast down:<- therefore, **Vulcan** is not to be separated from **Medicine**, but is to be most closely joined to it, just as a cook is joined to a kitchen. We have already related before that Vulcan has something in common with **Pallas** <note>The goddess Athena/Minerva, representing wisdom and craft.</note>, if not in physical union, then at least in the worship of a single altar. Let Pallas, therefore, govern Vulcan—that is, let premeditation and Wisdom govern the **Philosophical fire**. Concerning this fire, because it is manifold, we find it treated in many places. 

Nevertheless, according to these same witnesses, there is no doubt that all fires mentioned by authors can be reduced to four types: namely, **natural**, **unnatural**, **against nature**, and **occasioned** (or **Elemental**). For so says **Ripley** <note>original: *Riplexus*; referring to George Ripley (c. 1415–1490), an influential English alchemist.</note> in his third "gate": 

> "There are four kinds of fires which you ought to know: natural, unnatural, and against nature, and the Elemental which lights wood. We use these fires and no more. The fire against nature ought to torment the bodies; it is the **Dragon**, as I tell you, burning violently like the fire of hell. The fire of nature is the third **menstruum** <term>menstruum: a solvent used in alchemy to dissolve solid matter</term>; that fire is naturally within each thing. We call the 'occasioned' fire 'unnatural,' such as the heat of ashes and baths used for **putrefaction** <note>The alchemical process of breaking down a substance through gentle, moist heat.</note>. Without these fires, you will bring nothing to putrefaction so that its matter may be separated, and it may be simultaneously proportioned for a new conjunction. Therefore, make a fire inside your glass vessel which burns bodies more effectively than Elemental fire." 

These are his words, with which **Lully** <note>Ramon Llull, a Majorcan philosopher and reputed alchemist.</note>, **Flamel** <note>Nicolas Flamel, the legendary French scrivener and alchemist.</note>, and the ***Philosophical Scale*** <note>original: *Scala Philosophorum*; an alchemical treatise.</note> (Step 1), and others agree. Therefore, by Vulcan we properly understand the **occasioned** or **unnatural** fire and the **Elemental** fire, but not the natural fire. However, we add that the **fire against nature** must be prepared by Vulcan himself; if you recognize this, you possess half of the **Philosophical work**.

He is said to have lived in **Lemnos** because it is well known that this island possesses earth that is warm and primarily medicinal <note>Lemnos was famous for *Terra Sigillata* (Lemnian Earth), a medicinal clay used since antiquity as an antidote to poison.</note>. The smith's works which he made are partly **philosophical** <note>In this context, "philosophical" implies alchemical or hidden secrets of nature.</note> and partly of another intention, if they are considered more attentively. He made the shields and weapons of the **Gods** and **Heroes**, and distributed their insignias, because all their motion and power proceeds from fire; hence they are what they are, or are held to be so. To **Jupiter** he gave the scepter and thunderbolts, to **Mars** a shield, to **Neptune** a trident, and to others he gave other works of his art...

<margin>Apollo or the Sun. 5th son of Jupiter.</margin>
But **Herodotus** writes in *Euterpe* <note>The second book of Herodotus's *Histories*, which focuses on Egypt.</note> that they say Apollo and Diana were the children of **Dionysus** and **Isis**, and that Latona was their nurse, since she saved them; for Latona, being one of the eight [original] gods of the Egyptians, saved Apollo (who had been entrusted to her by **Ceres**) when she protected him on the island of *Phloë*—that is, the "floating" island—from the assault of **Typhon**, who was searching for the children of **Osiris**.
<margin>Four Apollos according to Cicero.</margin>
**Tullius** <note>Marcus Tullius Cicero.</note> enumerates four Apollos in Book 3 of *On the Nature of the Gods*. The most ancient was born of **Vulcan**, the guardian of Athens; another is the son of **Corybas** in Crete; the third is from Jupiter and Latona; and the fourth, called **Nomion**, is in Arcadia. To the third, however, as he is the most famous, all the great deeds and the many children sired by various concubines are ascribed. But if we consider the matter as it truly happened, or according to its nature, neither Herodotus nor Cicero would have had need of that distinction. And it is all the same from whom Apollo is said to be born, since he is at least a **Hieroglyphical persona** <term>Hieroglyphical persona: a symbolic figure used in ancient philosophy or alchemy to represent a specific substance, force, or quality rather than a literal deity.</term>, which finds no place in physical substance, but only in quality or relation—unless we prefer to treat them as "second notions" <note>A term from logic referring to abstract concepts derived from other concepts.</note>. The sense is the same whether Apollo is said to be born of Latona, or of Isis, or of Osiris, or of Jupiter; for Osiris and Jupiter, and Isis and Juno, are in reality one and the same. Nor does it matter whether Latona is established as the nurse or the mother of Apollo; the office is the same. But if we look at the suitability of the matter, the opinion concerning the nurse is more approved.

Yet, because it has been so widely accepted, we establish Latona as both the mother and nurse of Apollo and Diana. The Pagans determined nothing for certain regarding Apollo and the **Sun**, or Diana and the **Moon**—whether they are the same persons, or others, or different; and whether they were on earth or in heaven; whether they are those lights of the sky, or truly were Heroes of the earth.
<margin>Five Suns according to Cicero.</margin>

# Book 3 of Hieroglyphics

<page-num>122</page-num>

...he is said to have been the son of **Ether** <note>The personification of the "upper air" or bright sky</note>; another was the son of **Hyperion**; the third of **Vulcan**, son of the **Nile**, whose city the **Egyptians** claim is the one called **Heliopolis** <note>Literally "City of the Sun" in Greek</note>; the fourth is he whom **Acanto** is said to have borne at **Rhodes** in heroic times, the grandfather of **Ialysus**, **Camirus**, and **Lindus**; the fifth is he who is said to have fathered **Aeetes** and **Circe** at **Colchis**. Anyone, unless they are blind, can see that all these names are inventions, attributed by different poets to different things, persons, and places. Yet it pleased the **Pagans** <note>original: *Ethnici*; meaning the non-Christian peoples of antiquity</note> to seek a remedy for their superstition in this way, so they would not have to attribute many different parents and homelands to a single God. 

But if they say all these were Gods, where then did so many Sun-gods remain? If they were the lights of Heaven and identical to the celestial Sun, perhaps when they grew old they were heaped into one place, their light extinguished? If they were Kings and men, why are they called Gods, or said to have performed the deeds of Gods? For the name of the **Sun** <note>original: *Solis*</note> could not make them Gods, nor could the adulteries ascribed to many, nor other crimes and wicked deeds, which—if taken literally or historically—prove they were not even men, but scarcely half-men; they were far from deserving the name of Gods. 

Therefore, although four **Apollos** are established and five **Suns**, born of different parents and places, there is nevertheless one **Hieroglyphic person** <note>A symbolic figure used in allegorical or alchemical teaching</note> known not to Pagan writers, but to Christian artists and Physicians, born of **Osiris** and **Isis**, or even **Jupiter** and **Juno**, or **Jupiter** and **Latona**. 

<margin>
**Who can be called the Sun of Heaven.**
**Anaxagoras called the Sun a burning stone.**
</margin>

Meanwhile, through both Apollo and the Sun, the **Sun of Heaven** is commonly understood. And it is indeed the eye of the world, the Heart of Heaven, King of the **Planets**, the lamp of the earth, the router of shadows, the source of life, the maker of the day, the father of light, and the runner of almighty God; but by no means is it God himself. To deny that the Sun and Moon were Gods seemed irreligious to the Pagans, a crime to be punished by death. **Anaxagoras** <note>A pre-Socratic Greek philosopher (c. 500–428 BC)</note> was the first, despising the threats of false religions, to say the Sun was not a God but a fiery, burning stone. He demonstrated that the causes of **eclipses** <term>eclypsium; the darkening of one celestial body by the shadow of another</term> of the Sun and Moon happen by nature, and were not, as the Pagans thought, the sufferings and sicknesses of the Sun or Moon—to cure which they would beat bronze instruments to help <note>An ancient practice where people made loud noises during eclipses to "rescue" the sun or moon from being swallowed or to wake them from their "sickness."</note>.

Hence Ovid writes in the 4th book of the *Metamorphoses*: *“When the auxiliary bronzes of the moon ring out in vain”* <note>original: "Cum frustrà resonant æra auxiliaria lunæ." This refers to the ancient practice of clanging bronze pots during an eclipse to "help" the moon recover its light</note>. Whether **Anaxagoras** <note>A pre-Socratic philosopher who famously argued that the sun was not a god, but a mass of red-hot metal</note> understood the Sun analogically, as some wish to believe (implying that a "burning red stone" hinted at the **Philosophical Sun**), or whether he spoke to mock and elude the superstition of the common people, his opinion should be embraced. This is because it strips away all divinity from created things and the lights of the world.

<margin>The sons of Apollo.</margin>
Many sons are ascribed to **Apollo**: **Orpheus**, **Hymenæus**, and **Ialemus** by **Calliope**; **Delphus** by **Acacallis**; **Coronus** by **Chrysorthe**; **Linus** by **Terpsichore**; and **Aesculapius** by the nymph **Coronis**. They hand down the story that Apollo came to **Delphi** from the **Hyperboreans** <note>A mythical people of the far north, beloved by Apollo</note>, and the place was named after his son, **Delphus**. Regarding this location, the ancients spun a tale: when **Jupiter** wished to find the center and "navel of the earth" <term>navel of the earth</term><note>original: *umbilicum terrae*; the Greeks believed Delphi was the physical center of the world</note>, he released one eagle from the east and another from the west at equal speed. He commanded them to fly straight toward each other. When they finally met at Delphi, as an eternal memory of the event, a golden 

<margin>Delphi believed to be in the middle of the earth.</margin>
Eagle was dedicated. While this story is a mere fable and contains no truth—except perhaps to demonstrate that Delphi and the **Delphic Temple of Apollo** are at the "navel of the earth"—it reveals a poor understanding of geography. For in truth, every place is at the center of the world in that respect, because the body of the earth is a sphere, not a square or any other shape. But that most famous temple at Delphi, where in ancient times Apollo gave oracles and possessed an altar made of solid gold bricks—of which **Croesus**, the wealthiest king of **Lydia**, had sent a thousand—raised this place so high in honor and worship that it seemed to be the pinnacle of the world, 

<margin>A golden altar established for Apollo.</margin>
or the very center of the earth. The white one begins to appear on the surface of the waters at sunset, hiding itself until midnight, and afterward sinking into the depths. The red one, however, works in the opposite way, for it begins to rise over the waters at sunrise until midday, and afterward descends into the depths.”* These, therefore, are the two eagles that meet in the center of the earth, and there a golden eagle is set up as a monument.

Although others might interpret these things as pertaining to Magic or augury <note>the ancient Roman practice of divining the future from the behavior of birds</note>, as is perhaps possible, nevertheless—since Orpheus was not truly a magician, and even if he had been such a man or an augur—he could not affirm that he knew these things except **allegorically**. Thus they tell of **Democritus** <note>a Greek philosopher often associated in later traditions with Egyptian alchemy</note> that he understood auguries and the voices of birds, just as they also say of **Apollonius of Tyana**. They say that Democritus (who drew his doctrine from **Egypt**) was accustomed to name certain birds by a specific name, from whose mixed blood a snake would be born; if anyone ate of this snake, he would understand the language of all birds. And they recall that certain live snakes licked the ears of **Melampus** <note>a legendary healer and seer</note>, from which he is said to have afterwards understood the speeches of birds. 

Any person endowed with reason will be able to discern that such stories are utterly false if they are taken exactly as they sound. Hence **Cicero**, looking at the literal meaning of Democritus’s doctrine, said: *No man of greater authority has brought forth greater lies.* <note>original: "Nullum virum maiori authoritate maiora mendacia protulisse"</note> However, lest Democritus—whose wisdom and "golden sayings" **Hippocrates** admired and **Plato** delighted in—be held as such a liar, we shall preserve his honor through **Allegory**, as we do for Orpheus, Apollonius, and Melampus. 

We shall say that by "birds" and "winged creatures," and by "serpents," we are to understand the volatile and the shifting subjects of philosophy. For it is credible that if one "eats" the snake born from the putrefied blood of certain birds, the voices of birds do not remain unknown to him: for from "volatile" <note>in alchemy, substances that easily evaporate or change state</note> substances, through the putrefaction of the solution, there is made a firm and fixed substance called the **Fifth Essence** <term>Quintessence: the purest and most concentrated essence of a substance, sought by alchemists</term>. Since this essence is both "penetrating" and "liquefying," it is called a "snake." This snake then causes the same "birds" (the volatile substances) from which it was formed to be perceived through a similarity of nature. By such Allegories...

His mother is said to be **Coronis**. It is told that after she had conceived by Apollo, she had an affair with another man and was slain by **Diana** <note>Apollo's sister, the goddess of the hunt.</note>. They maintain that his nurse was **Trigone**, and that he was raised by **Chiron the Centaur** <note>A mythological creature, half-man and half-horse, famous for his wisdom and skill in the healing arts.</note> and educated by him; it was from him that he learned the art of healing. He was first called **Apius** (the Greek word <note>original: ἤπιος (hēpios)</note> signifies "gentle" or "soothing") because he would soothe the pains of the sick with medications. But it is recorded that he was named **Aesculapius** (whom the Greeks call **Asclepius**) after he had cured a man named **Asclen**. They tell the story that **Hippolytus**, who had been torn apart by his horses, was restored to life by his skill. For this reason, it is said that **Jupiter** [the king of the gods] was enraged because a skill had been discovered by which men could be recalled to life, and he struck the inventor of the art with a thunderbolt; as **Virgil** relates in the seventh book of the *Aeneid*. When his father [Apollo] took this heavily and mourned greatly (his tears are believed to have been turned into <term>amber<gloss>electrum: a word used in antiquity for both a gold-silver alloy and fossilized tree resin (amber).</gloss></term>), he slew the **Cyclopes** with his arrows.

This is so evident that if only this remained from the most ancient monuments, it would still provide sufficient testimony for this **Golden Medicine** and for the vanity of **Pagan Theology** <note>The author argues that Greek myths were actually encoded alchemical instructions, making the literal "pagan" religion a misunderstanding of scientific truth.</note>. It is necessary, therefore, to burn that thing without fear until it becomes ash; which ash may be fit to receive the spirit, the soul, and the infused tincture.”*

**Aesculapius** <note>The Greek god of medicine, Asclepius.</note> therefore restores dead bodies to life through his art; because he moves those things which are imperfect, and as if dead from infirmity, toward health and eternal life. The reason for the names of his wife and children is evident; for **Iaso** <note>original: "Iaso"; from the Greek *iasis*, meaning healing.</note> is named from healing, and **Hygieia** <note>original: "Hygiæa"; from the Greek *hygeia*, meaning health.</note> from health. Indeed, why **Serpents** are under his protection is clear enough; because the double serpents—one of which is winged, the other without wings, or a double <term>mercurial substance</term> <note>A fundamental alchemical principle representing the fluid, transformative power of matter.</note>, male and female—are the beginning and the end of the work. Hence the **Dragon** watches over him and is sacred to him, just as it is to **Mercury** and other gods and heroes of this family for the same reason. This was held as such a certainty among the Gentiles that the ambassadors brought back **Aesculapius** the God to Rome in the form of a Serpent or Dragon when a great plague was raging there; this is narrated below in Book 4.

<margin>From Epidaurus.</margin>

Thus the **Devil** supports the superstition of the Pagans—he who deceived our first parents in that same form—by shaping himself into a Dragon so that he might be believed to be **Aesculapius**. What some add concerning the eggs of a crow, from which **Serpents** were hatched by conspiring priests, perhaps holds true in this way: though it is a <term>hieroglyphic</term> <note>Here used to mean a symbolic or hidden truth rather than a literal historical event.</note> and not a historical thing, that **Aesculapius** was produced from a crow’s egg. For this is the **philosophical egg**, blackish and abounding with many superfluities, from which our **Aesculapius** must be separated. For thus says **Arnold** <note>Arnold of Villanova, a 13th-century physician and alchemist.</note> in the place cited shortly before:

> *“Because the aforementioned black earth,” he says, “is separated from the mixture during calcination <note>The process of heating a substance to high temperatures to purify it.</note>, which otherwise was inseparable in the whole work due to its very strong union; and therefore it was necessary to be separated by the most powerful artifice. For if it remained mixed, it would prevent the entry of the pure matter because of its own impurity.”*

These are his words. But **Lull** <note>Raymond Lull (Ramon Llull), a Majorcan philosopher and reputed alchemist.</note> shows that our medicine, once elaborated to that point, further possesses the form of an egg, when he says in his book on the <term>quintessence</term> <note>The "fifth essence," the purest and most concentrated form of a substance.</note>, Distinction 3, part 2: *“When it has cooled,” he says, “the artist will find our infant round, after the fashion of an egg, which he should extract and clean, etc.”* And in the *Tree of Philosophy*, under the 11th principle: *“After the rising of that color, it begins to gather in the middle in a round form, after the fashion of a most round moon, contained in a circle.”* **Aesculapius** extracted from the ashes of **Chiron** <note>The centaur who tutored Aesculapius; here Chiron represents the "manual operation" or the labor of the alchemist.</note> or the operation of the hands.

We have already touched upon how the sister brought aid to her brother as he was being born and acted as a midwife for her mother **Latona**. The reason for this matter is quite clear: for Redness <note>term: **Redness** (Latin: *Rubedo*). In alchemy, this is the final stage of the "Great Work," representing the perfection of the stone.</note> must follow Whiteness <note>term: **Whiteness** (Latin: *Albedo*). This stage follows the blackening/purification stage and precedes the final reddening.</note>, and not the other way around, as all the **Philosophers** <note>The author uses "Philosophers" to refer to alchemists or "natural philosophers."</note> testify. Furthermore, **Diana** vowed perpetual virginity and obtained it from her father **Jupiter**, specifically because she was deterred by the danger of the birth at which she had assisted. For the appearing Whiteness must not be removed, but "cooked" until it reaches Redness; and for this reason, she is said to remain a virgin <note>In alchemical allegory, the "White" stage must remain pure and "untouched" (virgin) while it matures into the "Red" stage.</note>. She was always depicted as a huntress with a bow and arrows, with which she transfixed **Orion**, the greatest hunter, out of envy and at the instigation of **Apollo**, while he was swimming in the waters—though she was unaware of what it was she struck. They also called her **Cynthia** after the very high mountain of **Delos** where she was born, and they believed her to be both male and female at the same time, as **Orpheus** says in a hymn: *Increasing and decreasing, the same is both female and male.* <note>original: "Aucta & deficiens, eadem quoque fœmina masq;"</note> **Alcman Melicus** <note>A 7th-century BC Greek lyric poet from Sparta.</note> considers her the wife of the **Air**, by whom she conceived and bore a son, **Dew**. **Marcus Manilius** <note>A Roman poet and astrologer from the 1st century AD.</note> imagines her being carried in a two-horse chariot (*biga*) and not a four-horse chariot (*quadriga*) like the **Sun**. And that famous writer of hymns, **Homer**, writes that she puts on and takes off splendid robes whenever she wishes, and bathes in the ocean, appearing now bright and now dark according to the splendor of her garments; 

<margin>The three Dianas of **Cicero**.</margin>

they say her chariot is drawn by white stags. **Cicero**, in the third book of *On the Nature of the Gods*, established three **Dianas**: the first the daughter of **Jupiter** and **Proserpina**, who is said to have fathered the winged **Cupid**; the second and better known, whom we have heard was born of the third **Jupiter** and **Latona**; the third’s father is recorded as **Upis**, and her mother **Glauce**—the **Greeks** often call her **Upis** after her father's name. **Latona** is the mother of her and **Apollo**, and this is most true: for **Lato** or **Latona** as she is called denotes one and the same subject. This is what **Morienes** <note>An influential, possibly legendary, early alchemist often cited in medieval Latin texts.</note> very frequently insists upon when he says:
> *Our **Lato**, although it is first red, yet it is useless, etc.* <note>original: "Noster quidem Lato quamvis primum sit rubens, tamen est inutilis, &c." In alchemy, "Lato" often refers to an alloy of copper or a specific state of the base matter.</note>

And: *If, however, the Laton <note>term: **Laton**. In alchemy, this refers to a base metal—often brass or an impure copper—that must be "cleansed" or whitened during the Work.</note> be burned with sulfur, etc. Likewise: when pure Laton is cooked for so long, etc.* And countless similar things may be seen in their proper places. **Diana** killed **Orion** with her arrows—that great hunter, the "Triple-Fathered" one <note>term: **Tripator**. A reference to Orion’s mythic birth from the hides of three gods: Jupiter, Neptune, and Mercury.</note>, the son of **Jupiter**, **Neptune**, and **Mercury**. After being blinded by **Oenopion**, **Orion** set out for **Lemnos** and was most kindly received by **Vulcan** <note>The god of fire and smithing, representing the alchemical furnace.</note>. **Vulcan**, taking pity on him, wished for him to be led to the rising Sun by his servant, where, restored to health, he recovered his sight. What help, I ask, would **Vulcan** offer **Orion** if not from his own art? <note>original: *ex arte suâ*. This refers to the "Art" of alchemy or metallurgy.</note> Therefore he sent him to the rising Sun; this is easy to understand and needs no explanation. **Diana** pierced this **Orion** with her darts while he was swimming in the sea, thinking she was aiming at a piece of wood. Now, **Diana** is both male and female; because she is of a hermaphroditic nature, since redness lies beneath whiteness, and from a female, a male is made in the Philosophical Mastery <note>term: **Magisterium**. The "Mastery" or Great Work of alchemy, specifically the perfection of the Stone.</note>. For so says **Senior** <note>term: **Senior Zadith**. The Latinized name of the 10th-century alchemist Muhammad ibn Umail al-Tamimi.</note>: *This is the power of the female, which he had made female in nine days; it signifies the soul, which is the power of the female, which they made male when it is coagulated and fixed in the fire, and it becomes a hot and dry male through that which it acquired from the fire's part; and it is then called male, and they name this coagulated water by the name of any male: then they wed her, and he is from her, and he is her root and her coagulation.* **Diana**, or the **Moon**, has the dew as her son, even though she is established as a virgin: because it is necessary for the dew to fall before her rising. She uses a two-horse chariot <note>original: *bigae*</note>, not a four-horse one, because she makes at least two colors appear—blackness and whiteness—and she possesses three elements; the **Sun**, however, requires all four colors and all four elements, if the authors are to be believed.

**Mercury**
7th son of **Jupiter**

**Jupiter** also conceived **Mercury** by **Maia**: He is depicted as the most vigilant of the gods. ...us, in Book 1 of *Astronomical Matters*, writes in these verses:

> You, Mercury <note>original: "Cyllenie," an epithet for Mercury based on his birthplace, Mount Cyllene</note>, are the leader and author of such great sacred knowledge;
> Through you, the inner Heaven is now known, and the stars recognized, etc.

<margin>Note.</margin>
The same Poet attempts to show that the entire foundation of religion among the Egyptians was first discovered by Mercury, along with the rites of sacred matters and the causes of natural things. From these, what else shall we conclude but the axiom—often repeated under the Egyptian Hieroglyphs—that all things depend on Mercury, and that he is the master of all things? His thievery is all too well known to those who have undertaken to work with any kind of Mercury; for this reason, he stole the tools from **Vulcan** and the other gods. But why is he said to be raised by **Vulcan**? Because he is Vulcan’s own disciple, and Vulcan is his teacher. His duties are well established; for Mercury <term>Mercurius</term> is named as if he were "the runner in the middle" <note>original: "medius currens," a popular but scientifically incorrect etymology in the Renaissance</note>, because he served at the feet of the Gods. Thus, in the Philosophical Art <note>A common term for Alchemy</note>, he runs through the beginning, middle, and end. He discovered musical instruments and intervals because all things are made by weight, number, and measure, from which eventually a specific sound emerges. He turned **Battus** into stone and slew **Argus** with a stone. It is no wonder, because Mercury—or the Index <note>a signpost or boundary marker</note>—at the crossroads is sometimes made of stone himself. To the Egyptians, he is the author of every discipline, as has been frequently stated; but regarding what would be a sin to name, he reveals that the secret Egyptian rites proceeded from Mercury, were instituted concerning Mercury, and were wrapped in silence. An evident proof of this—

These points, beyond those previously set out, explain the nature of Mercury quite clearly, and why he was employed in sacred rites and believed to be a God; for this nature is derived from the principal **Hieroglyphics** of the Egyptians and Greeks. Therefore, his festivals were celebrated in silence by initiates and sworn persons, so that they might not reveal anything to any other person. Hence, Lactantius, in his book *On False Religion*, argues in vain that Mercury was a man of singular talent and wisdom. This was not because it was evil in itself to name the believed gods, but lest the secrets lying hidden under the names of those gods and their rites should become known. This was the sole and proper reason why the initiates were chosen and sworn—those who would celebrate those rites and see the sacred statues—and why it was forbidden to divulge anything about the gods or sacred things, or to name the gods themselves.

Hence, certain common and general names were attributed to those gods to designate their supreme dignity, such as **Axioerus**, **Axiocersa**, and **Axiocersus**; these correspond to **Ceres**, **Proserpina**, and **Pluto**. **Ceres** is the same goddess for whom the **Eleusinian mysteries** were established, of which we shall speak below in the following book; and **Pluto** is the subterranean god of riches, of whom we spoke above. **Mercury** is added to these as a minister, who is "All in all." They tell stories that **Ulysses** <note>Odysseus</note> was initiated into those rites, for so it pleased **Homer**; purple ribbons, however, and not white ones, were used in those rites. Since Ulysses erred regarding them, they became the cause of the many wanderings and storms sent upon him during his return, from which he was nonetheless saved.

A very famous mountain has, upon its ridges, very cold fluids dripping from the rock; this water is called **Stygian water** <note>original: "aqua stygia." In mythology, the Styx was the river of the underworld; its water was often described as poisonous or possessing supernatural properties.</note>, in which no vessel of silver, bronze, or iron can endure without being consumed and eroded. It was believed that nothing could contain it except a **mule’s hoof**. 

Mercury is called "of the Sea" (*Marinus*), as others have thought, because he carried out the commands of the Gods by sea; "of the Heavens" (*Coelestis*) through the sky; and "of the Earth" (*terrestris*) through the earth. However, we know that in him exists that which is above and that which is below—the **Heaven and Earth of the Philosophers** <note>A reference to alchemical theory, where "Mercury" represents a bridge between the spiritual/celestial and the material/terrestrial realms.</note>—and because the earth is a participant in the water, he is said to be of three natures. This is either because he consists of water and earth as his own visible elements, and furthermore a "fifth essence" <term>Quintessence: the pure, celestial fifth element beyond earth, water, air, and fire</term> or hidden heavenly virtue. From the union of **Hecate** <note>A goddess of magic, crossroads, and the underworld, often depicted with three forms</note> with this threefold matter, she gave birth to sons.

<margin>It was a crime to name Mercury as Trophonius.</margin> 

Why the Athenians performed such solemn rites for the "Earthly Mercury" (called **Trophonius**) using all kinds of seeds mixed and cooked together in a single pot is a wonder, and it reveals Egyptian rituals. From what has been said so far, one may reason about these matters.

<margin>Mystical things.</margin> 

A mystical cause is also observed to underlie the days of the month dedicated to Mercury. From this, it seems the Roman custom of numbering the seven days of the planets began; for among them, just as even now, the first and seventh days are assigned to Apollo <note>The Sun</note> and the fourth day to Mercury <note>Wednesday, or "Mercurii dies"</note>, though no longer with respect to the age or movement of the Moon as in the past. 

It has already been declared quite often that Mercury explained to men the laws he borrowed from Jove and Pluto, the God of Riches.

<margin>The tongue is sacred to Mercury, as the messenger of silence.</margin> 

The tongue is sacred to him—not, as has been thought until now, as the God of Eloquence, but as the **God of Silence**. His sacred mysteries must be kept quiet, suppressed by the tongue within the "fence of the teeth" <note>original: "intra dentium vallum." This is a classical poetic metaphor for the mouth.</note>. For this reason, in the external ritual, the tongue was the last thing thrown into the fire. Because he was believed to be the messenger of silence for the gods, he is imagined to have had a daughter named **Angelia** <note>From the Greek word for "messenger" or "news"</note>. We shall speak of his image among the **Eleusinian mysteries** later.

<margin>Mercury imposed himself upon the world.</margin> 

This, therefore, is that Mercury who established his laws, sacred rites, ceremonies, and worship throughout every part of the world. <meta>This page continues the exploration of Mercury’s identity, moving from his elemental nature to his historical and mythological origins among various nations, specifically linking the Egyptian "Theut" to the Germanic and Gallic peoples.</meta>

<page-num>142</page-num>
<header>Book 3 of the Hieroglyphics.</header>

Through the most secret art then known to them, he nevertheless ruled, ordered, fixed, and un-fixed all worldly things, like an earthly God. From Egypt, he penetrated into Phoenicia and to the Greeks with his mystical religion; from them he passed to the Romans, who gave Mercury and his kindred Gods to almost the entire world over which they ruled, commanding them to be observed. In this way, the Spaniards, Gauls, Germans, Britons, and other peoples offered sacrifices to Mercury, as they did to Mars, as is evident from ancient histories. 

Although I suspect that the Germans drew their worship of Mercury from the Egyptians themselves—since they hardly cared much for Roman names or deities under a rule that was barely confirmed for so many centuries—for the reason that the Egyptians called Mercury *Theut* <note>The author is connecting the Egyptian god Thoth (Theuth) with the Germanic roots of "Teuton."</note> in their own language. The Germans, who perhaps called themselves *Theutons* or *Teutschen* <note>German: *die Deutschen*</note> after the worship of Mercury, worshipped Mercury in the forests together with Mars long before the arrival of the Romans in Germany. 

I am not unaware of what others bring forward regarding other reasons for his name, nor do I much refute them, unless they are presumptions rather than proofs. Pliny (Book 4, Chapter 14) considers the Teuton peoples of Germany to be so named after the God *Teuton*, whom they believed was born from the earth; for Mercury is truly said to be born from the earth. So also was *Teutates* <note>A Celtic god often identified by the Romans as Mercury due to his role as a protector of the tribe and a traveler.</note>, the name once given to Mercury in the Gallic tongue, who was also worshipped by the Gauls and appeased with human blood; hence the poet Lucanus says:

> *And those by whom cruel Teutates is appeased with dreadful blood;* <note>Original: "Et quibus immitis placatur sanguine diro Teutates." From Lucan's *Pharsalia*.</note>

Aventinus <note>Johannes Aventinus (1477–1534), a Bavarian Renaissance humanist and historian.</note> (Book 1) makes *Tuisco* a son of Noah, whom Noah had fathered in Armenia and sent into Europe, assigning to him whatever is contained between the Rhine and Tanais rivers. Others want Tuisco to be Ashkenaz <note>In the Table of Nations in the Bible, Ashkenaz is a descendant of Noah, often associated with the Germanic peoples in medieval traditions.</note>, the first-born son of Gomer, from whom the Germans are called *die Teutschen*. But since those things concerning the origins of nations are very uncertain and not most truly recorded in literature, we believe what we have received, or we receive it, although we do not believe everything.

In hermetic and alchemical literature, the "Cave of Mercury" often refers to a hidden place of transformation or the "interior" of matter.</note> from Orpheus and one of our own writers to those who inquire. For thus says *Orpheus* in his book on stones, while he [urges] men toward study...

These truly golden songs of a more recent "golden poet" <note>Referring to Joannes Aurelius Augurellus, author of the alchemical poem *Chrysopoeia*.</note> sufficiently explain what Orpheus understood by the "Cave of *Mercury*," to which he exhorts all wise men to travel for purification. For in this cave lives a golden Nymph called *Glaura*, who is herself *Mercury*; and just as there are many names for things in the world, she adopts as many metaphorical titles for herself so that she might not be seized by the unworthy.

Hence it is said in the *Turba* <note>term: *Turba Philosophorum* (The Assembly of the Philosophers) — one of the oldest and most famous Latin alchemical texts, presented as a debate between ancient philosophers.</note> near the end: *“Therefore, do not be deceived by the vast number of names, for he is dead even when he lives. But hold it as certain that he is that thing to which nothing foreign is added or introduced. Seek out his companion, then, and introduce nothing foreign to him, and let men multiply the names—for unless they were multiplied, even children would laugh at our wisdom.”*

Let us not care, then, for the countless modern names attributed to this material and subject. Among the most ancient authors, we say that this one and the same thing was called *Mercury*, and through it was understood Apis, all the bulls sacred to the gods, the other tamed dragons mentioned before, and nearly all the "hieroglyphic" animals and deities. Likewise, it includes all the monsters—the offspring of *Typhon* and *Echidna*—such as *Cerberus*, the *Chimera*, the *Sphinx*, the *Hydra*, *Hecate*, and *Geryon*; as well as all the lions, horses, birds, and beasts, some of which have been mentioned, while others will be discussed in their proper places.

Now we proceed to *Dionysus*, born to *Jove* from *Semele*, who is no less celebrated than *Mercury*. He is the same among the Greeks as *Osiris* is among the Egyptians and *Bacchus* among the Romans, as is clear from all the attributes assigned to him. Therefore, we shall now name him interchangeably as *Osiris*, *Dionysus*, or *Bacchus*, always meaning the one underlying subject, just as the ancients understood. *Semele*, the daughter of *Cadmus* and *Harmonia*, since she was a mortal and [beloved] by *Jove*, as they tell in the fables—

### Book 3 of the Hieroglyphics

...[Some have asserted] that *Semele* indeed bore *Liber* <note>original: *Liberum*; an ancient Italian deity identified with the Greek Dionysus or Bacchus.</note> to *Jupiter*, but having been caught with the newborn boy by *Cadmus* <note>The legendary founder and first king of Thebes.</note>, she was cast into a wooden chest. This chest was carried by the sea’s tide to the borders of *Oreatae* (which was a town of the *Laconians*), but when the chest was opened by the locals, they found *Semele* dead and buried her with great magnificence, while the boy was raised by them. However, *Meleager* believed that he was not sewn into *Jupiter’s* thigh, but was instead immediately snatched from his mother’s ashes and raised by the *Nymphs* themselves. *Demarchus* says he was raised by the *Hours*, and that this occurred in *Egypt*, as *Orpheus* maintains—though *Orpheus* was actually the first to say he was born at *Thebes*.

<margin>The Greeks talk nonsense to the Egyptians regarding Dionysus.</margin>
For this reason, those *Greeks* who say that *Dionysus* was born of *Semele* and *Jupiter* at *Thebes* appeared to be talking nonsense to the *Egyptian* writers. They claim this happened because *Orpheus*, having traveled to *Egypt* and learned the mysteries there, became a friend to the *Thebans* (who were descended from *Cadmus*). Wishing to please them, he invented these stories about *Dionysus*. The common people of *Thebes* easily embraced this—partly out of ignorance and partly because they wanted so great a God to be considered their own citizen—and passed it on to other nations as the truth. What is said here about *Dionysus* being falsely attributed to the *Thebans* by the Poets out of favor is the same thing we should assume happened with other gods and heroes, as we have warned before. Some have even said that *Dionysus* was born of *Jupiter* and *Ceres* <note>The goddess of agriculture and grain.</note>, and was torn apart and boiled by the "children of the earth" <note>likely referring to the Titans.</note>, but lived again as a youth after *Ceres* joined his limbs back together.

<margin>A miraculous event attributed to Dionysus.</margin>
Others say that the *Hyades* (whose name signifies rain) were the nurses of *Bacchus* on the island of *Naxos*. When he had grown to adulthood among the *Nymphs*, he performed many admirable deeds, which *Natalis Comes* <note>Natale Conti (1520–1582), an influential Italian mythographer whose works were standard textbooks in the Renaissance.</note> described in the fourth book of his *On Hunting* in this way:

> *Playing among these Nymphs, he happened to strike his staff,*
> *And with that same blow, the iron tip struck the stones;*
> *A stream of sweet wine leaped forth from the wound in the rock.*
> *Then he tore the guts of a sheep into pieces, with gore*
> *Staining the ground, and cast the limbs, white with bristles,*
> *Upon the earth; yet again, wondrous to say,*
> *The divided limbs of the beast suddenly came back together,*
> *And it began to pluck the green herbs, its familiar fodder.*

It is said that he killed an **amphisbaena** <note>original: *amphisbænam*; a mythical serpent with a head at each end.</note>—which is the name for a viper having a head on both sides—by which he had been bitten in the shin, using a vine shoot that happened to be lying nearby. It is also said that he called forth honey, milk, and other sweet liquids from the earth if he struck it with a rod. He is imagined to have been carried to heaven by **Jove** but was nearly cast down by **Juno**. **Ovid** called him "ever young" in the 4th book of his *Metamorphoses*; others have depicted him as bearded, and others as beardless. **Isacius** <note>Likely referring to Isaac Tzetzes, a Byzantine scholar known for his commentaries on Greek mythology.</note> testifies that the ancients believed **Dionysus** was simultaneously young and old, and **Orpheus** records that he was both male and female.

<margin>
Poetry is compared to the head.
</margin>
What some have asserted regarding the head of the **Polypus** <note>original: *Polypi*; likely an octopus or cuttlefish. Ancient naturalists believed eating it caused vivid or strange dreams.</note>—that it is indeed pleasant to eat but produces many fantastic dreams—others apply to **Poetry**. They suggest that poetry seems pleasant due to its fictions, much like the head of the Polypus, but it scatters many empty things similar to delusions. If this is true, it particularly applies to this allegory of **Dionysus** (or **Osiris**, or **Bacchus**), which encompasses his birth, life, and deeds. 

Truly, although some common things have been added to the deeds of **Dionysus** by poets of a later age, there remains no doubt that most things concerning the most secret matters of great importance have been transmitted and propagated down to us from antiquity within the wrappings of fables. For if the most ancient writers had attributed only the making of wine and the invention of the vine to **Dionysus**, and thus offered such significant things for the world to consider as are ascribed to him, they would be worthy of **Hellebore** <note>original: *Elleboro*; a plant used in antiquity as a treatment for madness; to say someone needs hellebore is to call them insane.</note> rather than Praise. The region was called the **Horn of Amalthea** <note>original: *cornu Amaltheæ*; this refers to the Cornucopia or "horn of plenty," a symbol of abundance associated here with a fertile territory given by Ammon to his mistress.</note>. However, **Ammon** <note>The Libyan deity often identified with Jupiter or Zeus.</note>, fearing the jealousy of **Rhea**, took care to have the boy brought to a certain city called **Nysa**, located far from those places. It was situated on an island surrounded by the river **Triton**, at a steep location where there were narrow passes they called the **Nysaean Gates**. The region there was very pleasant, distinguished by soft meadows, and the place abounded with many flowing, clear, gushing waters. It was planted with every kind of fruit-bearing tree, and many excellent vines also grew there of their own accord. The place was breathed upon by many most pleasant and healthful winds; therefore, the inhabitants enjoyed a very long life. The entrance to the region was fenced by many thick and tall trees and sufficiently deep valleys, so that the Sun could not easily penetrate, nor could even the light of the Sun itself. At all the approaches, there were springs of sweet water, and there were many trees that were always green and fragrant, sweet flowers, and the songs of various birds. To conclude in a word, nothing at all could be desired for the absolute pleasure of those living there.

Nysa, Aristaeus, and Pallas have the care of Dionysus.

But he put **Pallas** <note>Athena/Minerva</note> in charge of avoiding the snares of the stepmother <note>Rhea</note>. Because Pallas had been seen appearing from the earth a little earlier at the river Triton, she was called **Tritonia**. Indeed, when **Rhea** later heard the virtue and glory of her stepson **Dionysus** celebrated everywhere, she was angry with Ammon. She tried by every art to capture Dionysus, but when she was unable to do so, she left Ammon and fled to her brothers, the **Titans**, and decided to live with her brother **Saturn**. She even persuaded Saturn to undertake a war against Ammon along with the others, which was carried out. They say that Ammon, then suffering from a scarcity of provisions, was forced to flee to **Crete**. ### Book 3: Of the Egyptian-Greeks.

[Saturn] stirred up the hatred of his subjects against himself, and not much later, having assembled great forces, he went to war against **Nysa** and **Dionysus**. Dionysus, having heard of his father’s <note>Ammon’s</note> flight, gathered many soldiers from Nysa, and among these were two hundred infantrymen who were outstanding in strength, loyalty toward him, and service. 

<margin>
Dionysus's expedition.
</margin>
To these were added gathered forces from **Libya** and a great band of **Amazons** <note>The legendary warrior-women of Greek myth.</note>, who arrived all the more willingly because they understood they would have **Pallas** <note>Athena, the goddess of wisdom and war.</note>, who was eager for military matters, as an ally in the war. Thus, Dionysus led the army as the supreme commander of the men, and Pallas led the women. After the 

<margin>
Pallas, leader of the Amazons.
</margin>
battle began and many had fallen on both sides, **Saturn** was wounded, and the victory went to Dionysus, whose remarkable courage shone forth especially on that day. The **Titans** <note>The elder race of gods led by Saturn.</note> saved themselves by fleeing into the lands of **Ammon**; later, after they were captured through surrender, Dionysus restored them to liberty and gave them the choice of whether they wished to serve with him or depart. They all chose to serve with him and worshipped Dionysus as a **healing God** <note>original: *Deum salubrem*; a savior figure or one who brings well-being.</note>. They say the expedition against Saturn was undertaken with the most noble citizens of Nysa fighting alongside him, who were called **Sileni**, since the first man who reigned in Nysa was named **Silenus**. On the journey, he tamed many monsters and filled deserted regions with colonists.

Saturn, hearing of Dionysus’s forces, set the city on fire and, taking **Rhea** and certain friends with him, fled from the city under the cover of night. But when they fell into guards stationed everywhere and came into the power of Dionysus, they not only suffered nothing inhumane but were even voluntarily invited to live with him in the future out of fatherly affection, destined to receive all due reverence because of their blood connection. But when the Titans secretly prepared arms once again, they were defeated by him in battle and slaughtered to a man.
